text:
a sleep app asking how you feel in the morning is collecting a completely different kind of information from a wearable measuring how long you slept.

That distinction becomes important when an AI product tries to understand recovery.

Imagine two mornings.

On Monday, a wearable records seven hours of sleep. You wake up feeling rested.

On Tuesday, it records roughly the same duration, but you wake up exhausted.

From a duration-only perspective, those nights look almost identical.

From the user's perspective, they clearly weren't.

Sleepagotchi has a small product interaction that makes this difference worth examining: its Mood Check.

The interaction asks users how they feel, adding a self-reported observation to an experience that also includes sleep tracking and an AI Sleep Coach.

It's a simple input, but it represents a different category of information.

Wearable measurements describe what a device observed.

A mood check describes what the person experienced.

Neither automatically explains the other.

A device can estimate sleep duration, timing, and other signals, but it cannot directly measure every reason someone feels tired.

Likewise, someone reporting a bad morning doesn't establish that their sleep was objectively poor.

Stress, illness, workload, and circumstances outside the bedroom can influence how a person feels.

This creates a useful distinction for @sleepagotchi as it develops its Health & Wellness experience.

An AI coach needs to understand the difference between recorded sleep and perceived recovery before treating either as a complete picture.

The Mood Check also has a second role inside the product.

It appears as a recurring activity in Sleepagotchi's loyalty experience, where participation is recognized through points.

That introduces a behavioral-design trade-off.

Rewarding a check-in can encourage users to record how they feel regularly.

More frequent self-reports may provide a richer history of subjective experiences.

But a reward for submitting an answer doesn't guarantee the answer is thoughtful or accurate.

Someone might respond carefully because they want to understand their sleep.

Someone else might complete the interaction quickly because they want the associated points.

Both produce an entry.

Those entries don't necessarily have the same informational quality.

The design challenge is subtle: encouraging participation and collecting reliable personal context are related goals, but they aren't identical.

A good self-reporting experience should make honesty easier than optimization.

Users shouldn't feel pressured to report a better mood simply because the surrounding product celebrates progress.

And the application shouldn't imply that completing a check-in is itself evidence of improved well-being.

The distinction also affects how AI-generated insights should be interpreted.

Suppose someone consistently reports feeling tired after nights with irregular bedtimes.

That relationship might be worth exploring.

It still wouldn't prove that bedtime variability caused the fatigue.

The coach would need to present the pattern with appropriate uncertainty rather than converting a correlation into a diagnosis.

Now consider the opposite case.

Someone reports feeling well despite an imperfect sleep score.

A useful product should be able to acknowledge that experience instead of treating the device's interpretation as unquestionably correct.

This is where combining subjective and device-generated information becomes a product-design problem rather than simply a data-collection exercise.

Different inputs have different strengths.

They also have different limitations.

And combining them doesn't automatically remove those limitations.

Sleepagotchi's broader ecosystem positioning emphasizes consumer context, AI intelligence, and eventually more specialized everyday services.

The current sleep experience provides a concrete setting for examining that approach.

Before an AI system can offer genuinely relevant guidance, it needs to distinguish what was measured, what was reported, and what was inferred.

The Mood Check is a useful example because the interaction looks almost trivial from the outside.

A person opens the app and answers a question.

Yet that answer can represent something a sensor cannot directly observe: the user's own experience of the morning.

Whether that information becomes part of better coaching depends on how the product interprets it, not merely how frequently it collects it.

The goal should never be to make every morning look good on a dashboard.

It should be to help users understand why mornings can feel different, even when the numbers look similar.

This is my personal perspective and not a call to participate or invest.

𝗔𝗣𝗟 𝗔𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼 𝗧𝘂𝗯𝗲𝘀 𝗤𝟭 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟳

The company buys hot-rolled steel coil, bends it, welds it into hollow tubes and stamps a brand on it. Hot-rolled coil is flat steel sold in rolls, the raw sheet this industry starts from. The tubes reach more than 200,000 fabricators. They travel through more than 800 dealers and more than 50,000 retailers, across more than 300 towns. That is the whole machine.

The value added is not metallurgy. It is logistics, branding, and the ability to carry more than 5,000 product variants at once. The competing offer is whatever came out of the local melting shed that week.

Three product families do the work. Apollo Structural covers super-heavy, light and general construction. It includes India's first structural tubes made with direct forming technology, which shapes the tube without changing tooling for each size. The range also runs to door frames, planks, staircase steps and furniture tubes. Sizes go from 10 mm square up to 1000 mm square. Wall thickness runs from 0.5 mm to 40 mm. Apollo Z is rust-proof galvanised and coated high-tensile sections. It goes into coastal roofing, purlins, which are the beams that carry a roof, and factory sheds. Apollo Galv handles the corrosion-resistant end: greenhouses, plumbing and firefighting networks.

Housing took 64% of demand in the year to March 2026. Commercial buildings took 19% and infrastructure 13%. Other uses accounted for 4%.

Volumes in the three months to June 2026 split four ways. The APL Apollo brand shipped 5.69 lakh tonnes and roofing 91,516 tonnes. SG Premium shipped 58,686 tonnes and the UAE 25,929 tonnes. SG Premium is priced around ₹58,000 a tonne, some 6% to 7% below the flagship brand. Management is explicit that its purpose is taking market share from patra players. Its operating profit runs anywhere from nothing to ₹1,000 a tonne, depending on the local market. With the primary-to-secondary spread at ₹10 to 12 a kilo, Gupta's assessment is that "there is no benefit in selling goods by losing cash."

Value-added products were 58% of volumes in the year to March 2026. Management put the current share at "like 65%" and targets 75% to 80% by December 2027. Management links that to the new Malur plant, which it describes as "totally value-added", with a plant-level aspiration of "8,000 plus" operating profit per tonne.

The much-awaited Mangaluru Dasara celebrations are here! 🌺✨ The beautiful coastal city of Mangaluru has come alive with devotion, dazzling lights, vibrant cultural traditions and the festive spirit of Navaratri.

Mangaluru Dasara is one of the most prominent and widely celebrated Dasara festivities in Karnataka after the world-famous Mysuru Dasara. During this festive season, temples are beautifully decorated and illuminated, special poojas and cultural programmes are conducted and the entire city comes alive with celebrations.

🌺 𝗞𝗨𝗗𝗥𝗢𝗟𝗜 𝗦𝗥𝗜 𝗚𝗢𝗞𝗔𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗛𝗔 𝗞𝗦𝗛𝗘𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗔-𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨 𝗗𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔

The spectacular Mangaluru Dasara celebrations at Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra are among the biggest attractions of the festival. The beautifully illuminated temple, special religious rituals and cultural programmes create a magnificent festive atmosphere.

The worship of Goddess Sharada, Mahaganapati, Navadurgas and other deities forms an important part of the festivities. The grand Dasara procession on Vijayadashami is a major highlight, featuring beautifully decorated tableaux and idols, traditional chende, folk dances, Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, Gombe and the famous Pilinalike/Hulivesha.

🌺 𝗦𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗔𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗜 𝗧𝗘𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘- 𝗔 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗥𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗜𝗡 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨

The historic Shree Mangaladevi Temple at Bolar is another important centre of Navaratri and Dasara celebrations. The temple holds a special place in the history and identity of the city, with Mangaluru deriving its name from Goddess Mangaladevi.

During Navaratri, devotees visit the temple in large numbers to participate in special poojas and religious celebrations. The Vijayadashami celebrations and Rathotsava towards Marnamikatta are important parts of the traditional festivities.

🌸 𝗦𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗢𝗧𝗛𝗦𝗔𝗩𝗔 𝗔𝗧 𝗖𝗔𝗥 𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗘𝗧

The historic Car Street area has its own special charm during Navaratri. The traditional Sharadothsava at Acharya Math brings the area alive with devotion, religious programmes and cultural celebrations.

The worship of Goddess Sharada and the traditional procession through the streets of Car Street showcase the rich religious and cultural traditions preserved in Mangaluru for generations.

From the grandeur of Kudroli to the sacred traditions of Mangaladevi and the historic Sharadothsava of Car Street, Mangaluru offers a unique festive experience for devotees, tourists and families.

text:
Tanot Mata Temple in Jaisalmer, where 1965 war history meets faith.

Rows of bombs, now silent and preserved behind glass, stand as stark reminders of a war fought decades ago.

At the Tanot Mata temple, located in Rajasthan's Jaisalmer district close to the border with Pakistan, these remnants of the 1965 war have become part of a story that blends wartime history with deep religious faith.

During Navratri, as devotees gather to worship the Goddess, many visit this temple believing that she protected the area when bombs rained down from across the border.

After all, as local legend has it, not a single bomb exploded.

At this border shrine, the role of the Border Security Force personnel goes beyond guarding the nation, with its personnel also taking charge of the temple's daily rituals, from the morning aarti to the evening prayers.

For devotees, specially during Navratri, the temple is also a place to seek blessings and make wishes.

Many tie handkerchiefs at the shrine as a mark of their prayers, returning with faith that their wishes will be fulfilled.

Local legends trace the origins of this temple dedicated to Goddess Tanot Rai to the region's tribal communities.

With Navratri beginning, devotees are flocking to the revered shrine to offer prayers and seek the Goddess' blessings.

Adding to the festive spirit, the BSF is organising a community feast throughout all nine days of the festival.

By: Wish Fire

Ani Sun Magazine X Morning Star

In traditional Latin prayers and Christian symbolism, "doors" or "gates" (janua or porta) carry profound spiritual meaning. The Gate of Heaven (Janua Caeli)In Latin tradition, Mary is frequently invoked as the Janua Caeli (Gate of Heaven) because through her, Christ entered the world, opening the door to eternal life. The Homelessness Industry: Oregon Version

Cynical Policies in a Beautiful Place, Destroying Humans

By Dr. Naomi Wolf
Oct. 11, 2026

Human despair is being manufactured and monetized by corrupt health care organizations, in ways that defy belief.

Health care companies, working with the neoMarxists in Western blue states, are using local and state-level policies and numberless NGOs to produce ever more drug addiction, alcoholism, mental illness diagnoses, and homelessness.

This is the homelessness industry in Oregon.

I was in the Pacific Northwest about six months ago, in a bucolic little college town. It was the end of April. We were having a real, old-fashioned Spring. Days were warming; a faint sun was waxing steadier; the tiny leaves on trees, that had looked like a haze of veiling when I had first arrived, were emboldened; they grew into stubborn green nubs and eventually became vivid flags.

When I sat on the balcony with my beloved elder relative, massive rough-trunked trees shook down upon us a shower of seed pods like translucent coins; they spun in the sun as they descended.

Rhodedendra bloomed: the leaves were spearlike, a backdrop to the small heaping mountains of blossoms. These were deep-purple, or scarlet, or cream-colored with slate-grey centers. Peonies and irises, as various gardeners explained to me with the precision of those who truly loved their landscapes, would bloom the following week.

Everything looked as beautiful, as bucolic, as extremely friendly, as it always has.

But I noticed, as others may not notice if they are there every day, how much has changed since my last visit. And at that time, I had noticed how much had changed from the year before that.

The homelessness policy of the town is a perfect example of these changes.

I wrote in a former essay that I’d seen the tents of the homeless people steadily change locations.

At first the tents had been set up outside of town. Then they moved to an underpass separating the town from its outskirts, becoming a mini-neighborhood. Civic policy at that time had been to leave them alone.

Then the homeless population moved into the town itself; I wrote about how the town had in fact built tiny homes for the homeless, very pretty ones, located in a parking lot. I don’t know what became of that experiment, but each of these interventions did not seem to lessen the problem of homelessness, in this little town. On each visit of mine I saw the dwellings of what seemed to be an ever-increasing homeless population: and particularly, there were more and more drugged-out people, moving slowly due to their use of “tranq”.

This substance, also called “zombie drug”, or xylazine mixed with fentanyl causes the lassitude, and the immobilized, bowed posture, characteristic of many homeless people in American downtowns today.

I noted in my last essay the beautiful park in the center of town, one used by elderly people and children, with borders of rose plantings, a playground, and decorative statues, now housed a “free store” run by anarchists, which offered free clothing and other items, included canned and packaged food, at one entrance to this park.

Unsurprisingly, drug users were attracted to the “free store”, and several spend their time sitting on park benches, nodding off or slumped over, near the free items handout. A church facing the park had offered a free bag lunch to homeless people when I was last in town. Now, on this visit, I saw that it had extended its offerings of free food, and offered both lunch and dinner.

To my astonishment, on my last visit, a sign had gone up at the entrance to the park inviting the homeless people there to pitch their tents on one lovely, green, grassy oval. A Port-a-Potty had also been installed.

text:
Risk Rallies. Rates Stay High. | October 12, 2026
(📍Data From https://t.co/rtKhA53pFF Daily Report)

Stocks recovered. Precious metals rallied. The dollar held firm, and Treasury yields rose.

Friday’s combination suggests investors were willing to take equity risk while still paying for protection. It does not establish that inflation or financing pressures have eased.

The figures below describe October 9 closing snapshots—not live Monday prices.

1️⃣ Equities rebounded without help from lower yields

The Dow gained 0.83%, the S&P 500 0.59%, and the Nasdaq 0.64%. Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners on both major U.S. exchanges, providing some breadth behind the recovery.

Yet the bond market offered little valuation relief. The reported 10-year Treasury yield finished at 5.246%, up 1.3 basis points, while the two-year rose 3.6 basis points to 4.800%. The dollar index ended at 102.22.

Using those yield changes, the 10-year/two-year spread narrowed by 2.3 basis points. That modest flattening is consistent with greater pressure at the policy-sensitive front end, although it cannot identify the cause.

For equities, the implication is straightforward: rising prices must increasingly be supported by earnings expectations when discount rates remain high. A rebound can survive expensive financing, but it receives less support from valuation expansion.

2️⃣ Gold and silver strengthened despite those headwinds

Spot gold gained 1.47% to $4,194.45 an ounce, while silver rose 2.78% to $60.81.

Gold’s advance alongside a firm dollar and higher nominal Treasury yields deserves attention. It is consistent with demand for protection against inflation, geopolitical uncertainty or policy risk—but the price move alone cannot tell us which motive dominated.

Nominal yields also do not establish the movement in real yields, which require an inflation-expectations adjustment. Calling this a straightforward “rates versus gold” contradiction would miss that distinction.

Silver’s stronger performance adds volatility to the metals story. Its industrial exposure means the rally cannot automatically be interpreted as pure defensive demand.

The confirmation tests are real yields, ETF flows and whether metals retain their gains after this week’s inflation releases.

3️⃣ Oil’s modest gain concealed a significant regional disruption

WTI finished at $90.96 a barrel and Brent at $102.73. Hurricane Isaias prompted roughly 1.5 million barrels a day of Gulf offshore oil production to be shut in; reports put the regional shutdown share above 70%. That percentage refers to Gulf offshore output, not total U.S. production.

A large precautionary shutdown is not equivalent to permanent supply loss. As of Monday, major operators were preparing to redeploy personnel and restore production.

Watch restart speed, infrastructure damage and refinery operations. Offshore disruption constrains crude supply; refinery outages can also reduce crude demand while tightening fuel availability. The net effect depends on which facilities remain offline.

Friday’s closing oil prices therefore need to be distinguished from the evolving recovery story.

4️⃣ Hong Kong participated strongly; individual winners still need separate explanations

The Hang Seng gained 1.79%, and Hang Seng Tech rose 3.06%. Xiaomi climbed 9.72%, while several gold shares also advanced sharply.

The combination of technology and precious-metal strength supports a picture of mixed risk-taking and protection. It does not prove a lasting improvement in liquidity or earnings.

Moderna’s 14.21% U.S. gain was another standout. Such a large individual move requires its own catalyst analysis; it should not be used as evidence that the entire healthcare sector strengthened.

5️⃣ The next test is whether the recovery holds through new information

IMF–World Bank meetings begin today in Bangkok. The supplied calendar places Hammack’s remarks at 00:10 Beijing time on October 13.

Trader’s takeaway: Friday delivered an equity recovery, not a resolution of the macro risks.

The constructive path combines sustained market breadth, improving earnings guidance and normalization of energy supply. The adverse path combines persistent yield pressure, renewed disruption and weaker demand.

When stocks and protection rise together, conviction needs more evidence.

Azamara Cruises: The Destination-Immersion Cruise Line

Azamara occupies a unique niche in the cruise industry. While competitors often emphasize larger ships, onboard attractions, and family entertainment, Azamara's philosophy is built around"Destination Immersion®": spending more time in ports, staying later into the evening, and visiting smaller destinations that larger ships cannot easily access.

A Brief History of Azamara

Azamara was launched in 2007 as a premium small-ship cruise brand. Today the fleet consists of four sister ships:

Azamara Journey
Azamara Quest
Azamara Pursuit
Azamara Onward

These intimate vessels each carry fewer than 700 guests, creating a boutique-hotel atmosphere rather than a resort-at-sea experience.

Azamara's Approach to Cruising

The company's philosophy can be summarized in three principles:

1. More Time Ashore

Many Azamara sailings feature late-night departures and overnight stays, allowing guests to experience destinations after day-tripper crowds leave. The cruise line specifically promotes evening and overnight port experiences as a major differentiator.

2. Small Ships, Unique Ports

Because its ships are relatively small, Azamara can visit historic ports and smaller harbors where mega-ships cannot easily dock.

3. Cultural Immersion

Rather than relying on amusement-style attractions, Azamara focuses on:

Destination experts
Local performers
Cultural lectures
Authentic cuisine
Small-group shore experiences
Exclusive local events known as "AzAmazing Evenings"
Popular European Ports of Call

Mediterranean & Adriatic

These ports serve as major gateways for Azamara's European itineraries.

Included Excursions, Educational and Enrichment Activities
AzAmazing Evenings

One of Azamara's signature offerings is the complimentary AzAmazing Evenings program on many voyages.

These events may include:

Private concerts
Cultural performances
Historic venue access
Local music and dance experiences

They are designed specifically for Azamara guests and showcase regional culture.

Destination Speakers

Azamara regularly sails with destination experts who present talks on:

Local history
Archaeology
Art
Culture
Politics
Geography

The company reports having hundreds of destination speakers throughout its deployment.

Stories Under the Stars

An increasingly popular program, this outdoor evening event features local folklore, history, myths, and storytelling presented by regional experts on the pool deck.

Shore Excursions

Azamara offers thousands of excursions worldwide including:

UNESCO heritage tours
Culinary experiences
Wine tastings
Historical excursions
Archaeological visits
Small-group "Curator's Collection" experiences
Evening tours and overnight land programs

The emphasis is on meaningful cultural engagement rather than mass-tourism bus excursions.

Suite guests receive additional amenities, more space, and butler service in top suite categories.

What's Included in the Cruise Fare?

Azamara's inclusions are stronger than most mainstream lines but not quite as all-inclusive as ultra-luxury lines.

Typically included:

✅ Gratuities

✅ Standard spirits, beer, and wine

✅ Soft drinks

✅ Specialty coffees and teas

Typically extra:

Entertainment on Azamara is sophisticated rather than flashy.

Azamara's Key Differentiator vs. Competitors

The single biggest differentiator is:

Time in Destination

Azamara sells destinations more than ships.

Compared with competitors:

Cruise Line Primary FocusRoyal Caribbean Ship attractions and family entertainment
Norwegian Flexible freestyle cruising
Carnival Fun-focused vacation experience
Princess Traditional premium cruising
Celebrity Modern luxury ships and design
Viking Cultural enrichment and adults-only cruising
Oceania Culinary excellence
Azamara Maximum destination immersion and longer stays

Azamara's hallmark advantages are:

More late-night departures
More overnight port stays
Smaller ships
Access to lesser-known ports
Country-intensive itineraries
Strong cultural programming
Boutique-ship atmosphere

The result is that guests often spend significantly more meaningful time in destinations than they would on most mainstream cruise lines. For travelers who view the ship as a comfortable base from which to deeply explore destinations, Azamara is widely regarded as one of the strongest choices in the premium cruise market.

Ideal Azamara guest: a well-traveled couple or solo traveler who values culture, history, food, wine, and authentic local experiences more than large-ship attractions such as waterparks, casinos, and Broadway-style spectacles.

text:
My father was the sort of man described in the article below; a guy who knows how to fix anything.   
 
Since I left the farming community to take the college/law school path, I failed to assimilate his lifetime of experience and practical knowledge. 

I was shocked when, after a few  years away, I realized that my father and my baby brother were treating me like a city boy when I offered to help them with something.  

Apparently, in their pragmatic judgement, eldest son and big brother had lost a step.  

Despite my fall in status in the company of real men who work and fix stuff for a living, among my city based friends and neighbors with various degrees, I am regarded as something of a find - a guy who knows how to fix some stuff.  Pre-college time working with Dad had at least inculcated his problem solving methodology into me, even though I lacked his lifetime of experience.

The article made me think about men like my father and my limited experience with him.  

I came away with the feeling that we are on the verge of losing something that was a key factor in making us  who we are and has been part and parcel of our everyday lives.  

In our modern lives of degrees and affluence, have we lost our capability not only to fix anything but in a broader sense to take care of ourselves and our needs in our daily lives, i.e. to be self-reliant?  

The Last Man Who Knows How to Fix
 Anything How We Became the Most Educated Idiots in Human History
abstractruth  Oct 9   

  Frank is retiring. He lives in Bakersfield, California, is 73 years old and is known as the guy who can fix anything. He works mostly out of his garage, still carries a flip phone, listens to AM radio, and has a vinyl record collection that he never stopped listening to, even now that it is hip again. He plays guitar and a little banjo, and is looking forward to spending more time hanging out at the country music places in Bakersfield, where he meets up with his friends every couple of weeks. Frank’s retirement would not be a big deal, other than the fact that he has no replacement.
 
Frank doesn’t have a personal brand, has never attended a leadership seminar, and wouldn’t know a disruption consultant if one backed into his garage. But if your furnace breaks down in January, Frank is probably the guy you want to know. Modern-day America is the most credentialed place on the globe. And there isn’t anyone who actually knows how to do anything.We have so many experts that it is hard to keep them all straight. There are personal branding consultants, thought leadership strategists, life coaches, mindfulness consultants, corporate storytelling specialists, and disruption consultants. We should probably describe a few of these expert fields for those of us who are still trying to understand how we acquired all of these experts.Because I am currently working with digital companies, I have learned that there are such things as disruption consultants. These are really important people. Following up on the strategists in Silicon Valley who want us all to “move fast and break things,” the disruption consultant is someone who advises businesses to “disrupt” their industries. It matters not that these experts usually know precious little about the industries in which they advise their clients. I suppose that doesn’t matter if you are simply telling them to become a disruptor. Innovation used to be reserved for people like Thomas Edison, Alexander Graham Bell, and Beethoven. But now everyone is an innovator.This probably accounts for the abundance of “labs” out there in commercial America. A place where you used to buy shoes was usually called a shoe store. Now it’s a “shoe lab.” The 19-year-old kid who can’t remember where he put the size 10s because he was out back smoking weed is no longer some stupid kid. He is now a laboratory specialist. I suppose the guy who owns the store is “disrupting” the marketplace by selling shoes, while the kid who can’t find your size is conducting research.
 
Because I live in Los Angeles, I am surrounded by all kinds of experts. There are life coaches. These are people hired by Bobby’s parents in Brentwood to tell Bobby to wake up earlier, think about getting a job, stop drinking beer before noon, and establish the goal of one day actually getting a job. Thurston, the life coach, then reports back to Bobby’s parents on his progress. These are the kinds of things that my mother used to say to me when I was eleven years old while she was making me lunch. But she didn’t make $500 an hour. It’s unclear whether my father was a life coach when he would wake my brother Paul and me up at 7 a.m. on a Saturday and tell us to get the hell out there and shovel the https://t.co/kLvUWUgAEo of my favorite experts these days is the employee engagement architect. This is someone who designs an elaborate program to determine why employees are unhappy at a cost of $300,000, while avoiding the possibility that they might simply want fewer meetings and to be paid more.Another Los Angeles innovation is the “authenticity coach,” who charges exorbitant sums to convince people to “be themselves,” as if they had the choice to be someone else. There are also “personal branding coaches,” although here it is equally unclear why a thirteen-year-old girl who still rides her bicycle needs a personal brand.
 
For shop owners and restaurateurs, there are vibe creators. These are highly paid individuals who determine whether a hotel, restaurant, or workplace has the proper atmosphere. This job was previously occupied by unpaid personnel known as “customers with an opinion.” If you are lucky, you might run into an “innovation evangelist.” This is a person who attends conferences to explain to the audience why innovation is important, without the benefit of ever having invented anything.If all of this sounds fake to you, it is. But this is Los Angeles. Still, there are equally gifted experts on the East Coast who continually advise on problems that no one has, in an effort to make people believe they have one so they can make a bunch of money. New York is filled with these people, but the punchline is always money. Your New York consultant charges you $800 an hour to explain why your authentic self is inadequately monetized. And so you can find strategic narrative architects, executive visibility consultants, and organizational transformation sherpas. Meanwhile, Frank is back in Bakersfield fixing somebody’s https://t.co/VSeaZxroZt my own case, I have eleven years of college but have to call my wife into the room when I want to build something from IKEA. And so we’re a bunch of bozos who have utterly forgotten how to build a civilization. The entire nation has become a bunch of third-generation trust-fund kids.
 
If we want to examine how we got here, it’s probably best to begin with our education, or lack thereof. These days, teachers’ unions, administrators, and half-wit politicians are busy degrading standards so badly that some education reformers have even managed to argue that traditional approaches to mathematics are racist. There was a time when high school might teach a young person how to use a lathe, rebuild an engine, wire a circuit, or build a cabinet. Before we began focusing on pronouns, we had shop class, auto shop, and home economics.Home cooking is so bad now that we treat a trip to Jack in the Box as one of the mysteries of the universe. Guys who used to be called cooks are now called chefs and don’t allow alterations to their pizza. Shop class was noisy, smelled of sawdust and oil, and forced the student to understand that building something took skill and effort, and that furniture was not constructed by anything other than hard work.The backwards hierarchy that crept into our schools was that clever children went to college while others learned to repair the things that the clever children would eventually break. We never stopped to consider that a skilled electrician understands a great many things that someone with a bachelor’s degree does not. An electrician can get the lights turned back on, while the guy with the bachelor’s degree can light a candle and read poetry.There is nothing wrong with reading poetry. I have spent a considerable portion of my life doing things that have absolutely no practical application, including studying philosophy and theology. But somewhere along the way, we decided that knowing how to work with your hands was evidence that you weren’t sufficiently intelligent to work with your https://t.co/VgL1MhB01f abandoned much of the ideal of educating the whole person that the Greek philosophers had set forward. I like to have a Manhattan on the rocks and discuss Kant with the best of them. But a true education ought to cultivate skill for the hands as well as the mind. The arms and legs are not just useless appendages. Knowing how to frame a door, make pottery, do mechanical drawing, construct a table or chair, or grow a garden are core skills that anyone starting a community should know how to do.Consider what it would take to build a community from scratch in eighteenth- or nineteenth-century America. You could not simply send to China for new stuff when something stopped working. First, you need water, food, and shelter. Someone has to clear the land, cut down trees, build houses, dig wells, plant crops, and figure out how to survive the winter. You would need a blacksmith to make and repair tools, carpenters to build things, a miller to grind grain, a shoemaker, and somebody who knows how to construct roads and build bridges.Then you would need to produce supplies of sufficient quality that you could trade the excess for other things you might need. There would have to be someone around who could teach children how to do these things, because if you couldn’t do them, no one could give a fuck what your pronouns were. When winter arrived and the food ran out, nobody was going to care about your personal brand, your lived experience, or your ability to facilitate a discussion about community resilience. There were no feasibility studies, no government grants, and no bottled water. There was work to be done, and if nobody knew how to do it, people starved.Communities were built by people who knew how to do things, not brand strategists, executive coaches, or social media influencers. Fighting fires, surviving the winter, and making sure that your kids didn’t starve to death were more important than microaggressions.There were no radio stations. If you wanted music or dance, you created it. If you were educated in the true sense, you not only knew how to do some of the aforementioned things, but you probably played an instrument or two, spoke a few languages, could grow your own food, milk a cow, make your own bread, or, if you wanted meat for dinner, went out and hunted for it. Even if you wanted to play an instrument, it was usually too expensive to buy one, so you made one. Some of the great Delta blues musicians began playing on homemade instruments. Even Beethoven understood enough about pianos to guide the instrument makers of his day.
 
Aristotle called the knowledge involved in making things techne, the practiced knowledge of how to do or make something. He also wrote about phronesis, practical wisdom, which is the judgment required to live well. Both require something more than an empty credentialization ceremony. If you are building a house, it has to be designed properly, the boards need to be cut just right, and the whole thing needs to hold together. None of this is going to improve simply because Murray the builder has a degree from Yale.Our education has done the opposite of making us self-sufficient. It has created millions of dependent creatures who literally could not survive in the wild. We have gone from one of the most resourceful civilizations in the last half millennium to one that flies into a panic when the Wi-Fi goes down or we have to wait an extra 35 seconds for our smartphone to make contact with the satellite.There is also the small matter of what happens when an entire country forgets how to manufacture the things it needs. Before the current administration turned its attention to fighting wars and protecting the deep state, it did have a few passing moments of lucidity. It was once intelligent enough to understand that it was a national security risk for us not to know how to do anything. It began making some strides toward bringing industry back to the United States. It raised the obvious point that we actually needed things like steel mills, automobile manufacturing, and prescription drug production rather than leaving that kind of stuff to countries that may not have our best interests at heart.But then the President became distracted by foreign adventures, and there was also the important issue of ensuring that his name appeared ahead of JFK’s on the former Kennedy Center. A man needs to have priorities, after all. So the work of bringing industry back to the United States, reviving the middle class, and making things affordable enough for people to raise families will apparently have to be reserved for someone else. The work of reforming our education system so that our kids actually know how to do something, reading, writing, arithmetic, building skills of self-sufficiency—those kind of reforms will have to wait for a political establishment that can see five feet ahead of itself on the road. We have managed to create a society in which almost everyone has an opinion about how the world should work, but fewer and fewer people understand how it actually does work. We can explain why something is wrong with society, organize a conference about it, hire consultants to examine it, and produce a strategic plan for fixing it. But when the toilet stops working, we have to call Frank. And now Frank is retiring. 
 
Frank and his pals belong to a generation that learned how to sharpen a blade, fix a lawnmower, repair a furnace, and play a few Hank Williams songs on the guitar. Some taught themselves to play instruments, and some even made their own. Frank and his friends, all of whom know how to do things, have been together for the better part of half a century. None of them were especially interested in changing the world, but the odd thing is that people like them did.They are the inheritors of the traditions of the men and women who built the Brooklyn Bridge and the Lincoln Tunnel, the Interstate Highway System, the railroads, the major cities and small towns, the farms that fed the country, the ships that sailed the oceans, and the airplanes that we ride on every day. They designed automobiles, constructed factories, and crafted the instruments that fill our orchestras. They did it without possessing prestigious credentials, or even the slightest sense that by carrying out the small tasks required to live in the world, one at a time, they were changing it.And perhaps that is what we have forgotten. There is dignity in knowing how to do something, and satisfaction in making something that works. Frank doesn’t need a consultant to help him discover his authentic self. He knows who he is because he knows what he can https://t.co/nmSloPHM5D while we all talk big about how we’re going to reshape the world, perhaps we had better get hold of Frank before he retires and ask him how to live in it.Because one of these days the lights are going to go out, the furnace is going to stop working, and our credentials aren’t going to save us. Only our humility will.

text:
Due to this year's permanent appointment exercise, Sabah lost 244 medical officers (MOs) because 333 transferred out of the state, but only 89 from outside Sabah reported for duty in that state.

Sabah's deficit of 244 MOs comprised 219 in hospitals and 25 in public health (district health offices and Klinik Kesihatan).

Out of 269 MOs posted to Sabah from outside, only 89 reported for duty (33%), 171 no-shows (64%), and 9 deferrals (3%).

Overall, 331 out of 511 MOs offered permanent positions in Sabah reported for duty (65%), according to JKNS data as of Oct 7, 2026.

All 242 MOs already serving in Sabah, who received permanent appointment offers in the same state, had reported for duty, even as only a third of doctors from outside Sabah reported for duty in that state.

Twenty-two public hospitals in Sabah suffered net MO losses. Only Kuala Penyu Hospital saw no change, while Tambunan had a net gain of 1 MO. Top MO deficits:
- Sabah Women and Children: -36
- Queen Elizabeth: -33
- Duchess of Kent: -26
- Tawau: -23
- Lahad Datu: -19

Out of 138 MOs from outside Sabah who were offered permanent posts in hospitals in the state: 80 no-shows (58%), 52 reported for duty (38%), and 6 deferrals (4%).

Five hospitals had 100% no-shows among MOs posted from outside Sabah: Papar, Tenom, Sipitang, Beluran, and Kunak.

Other hospitals with high no-show rates among MOs posted from outside Sabah exceeding 50%:
- Ranau: 86%
- Beaufort: 86%
- Tawau: 80%
- Kota Belud: 80%
- Pitas: 80%
- Kinabatangan: 80%
- Lahad Datu: 67%
- Kuala Penyu: 67%

A dozen public hospitals in Sabah are understaffed, following the 2026 permanent appointment exercise, based on available JKNS data on manpower needs in those facilities.

Five are running at below 60% operational capacity:
- Ranau (45%)
- Beluran (50%)
- Kudat (56%)
- Sipitang (56%)
- Kinabatangan (57%)

Based on JKNS data, the number of medical officers in Sabah dropped by 44% from 3,908 in 2021 to 2,208 in October 2026.

text:
so

the nature of god and of the universe created by god. first i must cover a bit of human history to put this in the proper perspective. in ancient times the notion of the separation of church and state were non-existent. that is a purely american concept that simply did not exist before the writing of the u.s. constitution. in ancient times the church and state were one entity. in the earliest tribal cultures this was expressed as the chief and the elders of the tribe. later it developed into the king and the church. the chief and later the king managed the material matters of the tribe, things like the enforcement of the laws, defense of the tribe, handling disputes between members, and dealing with matters such as gathering food and waste disposal and all the daily needs of the tribe. the elders dealt with the spiritual matters of the tribe, things like health and well-being, education, and training of the members in their assigned duties, and most importantly advising the chief in how to manage his authority and holding the chief to account in the exercise of that authority.

in those times there was no separation of the matters that we call science and religion. they were both considered spiritual matters and were the purview of the elders, with the chief acting as the authority figure exercising the will of the elders. as tribal societies began to develop and grow, they encountered other tribes that were set up in the same basic fashion, but there were differences in the details of the different systems, which regularly evolved into conflicts ranging from simple disagreements to full scale wars. this was because each tribe developed its own understanding of the forces of nature and their own methods of dealing with those forces. the tribes gave names to the forces and considered them the names of what eventually developed into the idea of "gods". the tribes, through the elders and the chief, assigned the forces personalities that were reflections of their ideas as to how such gods would think and feel based on their own thoughts and feelings regarding the forces, and individualized them into "beings" like themselves, but more powerful versions of themselves.

as the tribes developed these gods were worshiped, offered sacrifices, and pleas for things such as rain, warmth, food, and especially protection from the gods themselves. they saw themselves as powerless to the forces and created these ideas of gods to manage those forces and protect them from those forces, while simultaneously believing that the gods were the forces themselves, so they worshiped and sacrificed, begging the gods to have mercy on them and carry them through their encounters with the forces. the gods were seen as persons, but not as people. the people believed that they could entreat these persons to do their will, and when things went well believed that they had pleased the gods, when they went badly, they believed they had displeased the gods. worship and sacrifice then became both the means of giving thanks, and of essentially buying the favor of the gods. such worship developed into ceremonies, rituals, and idols, and the sacrifices were anything from food to human beings. everything was considered subject to being sacrificed to the gods as everything was considered as belonging to those gods.

as the tribes grew and began to wander about the world seeking greener pastures for their animals, and fertile soil for crops, they encountered other tribes doing the same. since each of the tribes had to compete for these spaces, and because each of the tribes had their own ideas of the gods, conflicts between the tribes developed along those two lines. the tribes battled over both the requirements of survival, and over their differing ideals. this is where the notion of "the chosen" came from and was the root of the conflicts. our gods are better and stronger, and our gods are the only true gods, and our gods can beat your gods, and therefore our tribe has the same relationships to your tribe. warring tribes always had a winner and a loser. the loser was always either destroyed by the winner, or they were enslaved by the winner. if the loser was powerful enough, they were destroyed, if they were weak enough, they were enslaved. this continued for centuries until the hebrew tribe came along with the notion of a single, all-powerful god that ruled over all of the forces.

of course, this notion was fought against as it ran contrary to "public opinion”, but it contained a component that had previously been left out of the recipe. this was the idea that each individual could entreat this one god for his own sake, and not just for the sake of the tribe. this was the birth of individual empowerment, and it began with the hebrews. where previously everything was based on the needs of the tribe as a whole, the hebrews gave birth to the notion that the needs of the tribe could also be served, and often better, by empowering the needs of the individual by allowing direct access to the one god. many gods could only be considered from the mindset of the many, but one god could be considered from the mindset of the one. eventually the idea of one god replaced the idea of many gods as the needs of the many became more and more dependent on the needs of the one.

the one god was still seen as a tyrant as were the many gods, but a single tyrant is much easier to sway than many tyrants. so god became the idea of the creator and the destroyer of all things and all people, rather than simply the personalities that managed the individual forces of nature. the elders, and eventually the church were the channel through which the gods were reached, so they then also were the ones through which the one god was to be reached, and they made sure that this arrangement maintained through fear, and that fear was also exercised over the chief, and the elders went from counsellors to the real power of the tribe, with the king being the enforcer of their will. this balance of power rocked back and forth over the centuries but eventually the elders became the power, and the chief the executive authority as the means to balance the equation.

all of this maintained for centuries; one tyrant of a god ruling over one tyrant of a church that ruled over one tyrant of a king who ruled over the people subjected to their wrath. since the church and the king were those who, though tyrants, were generally wise tyrants and knew that they had to provide their subjects with some relief from their tyranny, or they would rise up and destroy them and thus create anarchy. this was the birth of religion, and it was most prevalent and eventually overwhelmingly practiced by the hebrews. as long as the people did their jobs, gave their substance to the church, and especially followed the rules laid down by the church through the king, they could petition god for that relief. they could pray, as long as they did it the way they were told they had to do it. this maintained until along came the son of a carpenter who was willing to do what nobody before him had even considered; he was willing to be wrong.

jesus looked at the misery of the people and correctly deduced that it was due not to what the church taught, that such misery was deserved because the people were miserable sinners as they were taught by the church and king, but because of that teaching itself. he realized, faintly at first, the true relationship between god and man, and escaped the tribe for eighteen years to wander in the wilderness and through the world of the time, learning different ideas and pondering concepts that came to him due to that willingness to be wrong that we now call "having an open mind". the simple willingness to look at hard held beliefs and superstitions and ask, "what if i am wrong?" was something nobody had ever done before jesus, and very few have done since jesus. this is what made jesus the only begotten son of god; he was the only one who had or really ever has begotten god properly, and he ended up on the cross for that begetting.

jesus figured out early on that the ideas he was exploring were ideas that would shake the power structure to its core, and that that structure would destroy him for so doing, but once his eyes were opened he could not allow himself to close them again, regardless of the consequences. this is what made jesus unique. he was truly the first individual to actually put the needs of the many ahead of the needs of the one; himself. the idea of self-sacrifice was so foreign to human thought that it had never before been considered. life had always been about survival no matter what the cost, and the notion of putting that beneath knowing and then speaking the truth was unheard of. what drove jesus to do what he did was his character that developed from the curiosity of a young boy who innocently discovered a truth previously not considered since before the very idea of gods came into being.

this little boy looked at the world around him, and in his innocence he noticed things like the birds feeding on the seeds that grew wild without conflict and without lack. he saw the flowers growing without effort or direction from any authority. he saw the cooperative relationship of predators and prey not as a struggle to survive, but as a natural give and take between species. he saw that if there were no predators, the prey would quickly outgrow their food sources and eventually die off completely. he saw the predators battling to the death and realized that the battles always ended with the stronger being the victor, and therefore the seed for the next and stronger generation. jesus looked at the forces of nature around him and saw, not the exercise of tyrannical power of one over others, not the power of a tyrant over his subjects, but the presence of a loving father providing for his children. jesus was a true paradigm shift in human consciousness, because he realized the true relationship with god as "our father".

jesus then escaped the bonds of the set of experiences he somehow knew would overwhelm this fledgling idea and spent those years wandering the countryside learning all he could from the very people he was not supposed to associate with; all the other tribes in all the lands his feet would take him to. because the sun rises in the east, that is where his feet took him. he wandered all over asia, attending to one master after another steadily learning new ideas that, building on his opened mind, he developed into the set of concepts and practices that are laid out in the gospels. these were simple ideas that were actually based on the very flawed ideas he had rejected, but ideas that turned them around due to a simple realization he experienced due that open mind and what he fed that open mind. "what if i am wrong?" led jesus to realize that the world is actually completely backwards in every way that it looks at god and man. the world is 180 degrees out of phase with the truth. 

jesus realized the simple notion that the reason why people experience the misery they experience, is because the power of their attention is so focused on the misery, that they are incapable of doing that which would heal that misery. that is to take that attention off the misery and the problems that cause that misery and give it instead to the solution for the misery; "our father". jesus experimented with this revolutionary idea as he travelled about by simply redirecting his awareness from the misery his senses showed him, to his new idea of god. he wandered around the countryside, and he simply talked to god as he would talk to a loving father, asked god to provide for his needs, asked god to provide the answers to his questions, and spoke those things to god as he wandered alone. he filled his mind with the beauty of the natural world his senses showed him and focused his thoughts inward into this idea he had of god and told god the stories that came to him just as a child would tell daddy about the cool thing that happened to him today.

it did not take long, nor did it take much effort for jesus to begin hearing the voice in his head, that he knew was not his own, answering those questions, smiling at those stories, and loving every bit of them and him. he also noticed that as he was so focused on his father, his father made sure that things like food, water, and shelter including clothing appeared along his path in some form or another, and the only time he had any difficulty was when that focus was interrupted for any reason. what mattered was the focus, not the reason. jesus simply trained his mind to be laser focused on his idea of god, an idea of love, of life, and of liberty; and due to that he was loved, alive, and free. try to imagine feeling these qualities in every aspect of your own life. that no matter what may be happening in the world, the completely overwhelming feelings of being fully loved, completely alive, and absolutely free remain untouched. this is what jesus brought to his world, and for what he was eventually murdered, because he knew he had to give it in order to have it.

so let’s look at that "it" more deeply. to do this, the ideas of science and of religion must be reconciled. in the time of jesus, just as there was no separate notion of "church and state" there was no separate notion of "science and religion". the ideas we call "miracles and magic" were in the religion and science of the time, and to gain the understanding of them one only has to look to two books of the bible: genesis and exodus. specifically, the first three chapters of genesis, and the portions of exodus that deal with moses and his experiences with god and with pharaoh. in genesis we have the story of creation, and in exodus we have the story of the nature of god and the laws that flow from that nature of god. so let's begin with the beginning and that is the very first sentence of the bible. "in the beginning god created the heaven and the earth". ten simple words that reveal more than the volume of the letters can possibly contain.

if you ask most people what was the first thing that god created they will likely say "light" for that is what the book says, but in truth it was "heaven and earth" which when looked at in modern terms can be expressed as the idea of "cause and effect". heaven is cause and earth is effect. god is heaven and earth is the physical universe. how this expresses the nature of god can be ascertained by reading the portion of exodus where moses speaks to god through the form of the burning bush for the first time. after god tells moses what he must do; lead israel out of bondage and to the promised land, moses posits a simple but never before considered notion. when i go to the people to speak for you, they are going to ask for your name, so what is that sir? the answer he is given reveals the true nature of god as does the name of anything else. god's answer is simple; "I AM THAT I AM, TELL THEM THAT I AM HATH SENT YOU." boom! god in a nutshell. imagine a loving father answering the question posed by the simple mind of his child in this form; "I AM ME, SILLY BOY." 

“i am that i am” is the expression of pure, unconditioned being. god simply is, and nothing else matters to that simple truth. now, once you have the name and the nature of god, by simple inductive logic and the very words themselves you have the nature of man expressed as well. the offspring is "made in the image and the likeness" of the parent, so man too is essentially pure unconditioned being, and man expresses that idea with the words "I AM". think of your own life and look at all of the many different ideas that you assign to yourself by saying "I AM THAT". i am male, or i am female. i am healthy or i am sick. i am alive or i am dead. i am this and i am that and i am and i am and over and over and over we repeat this process mindlessly and without understanding that with each utterance of any form (the form matters not to the content) we are actually invoking the name of god into our own existence. "I" is cause and "AM" is effect, heaven, and earth. content determines form; content being consciousness expressed as thought and emotion, form being the body and the body of material experience; the physical universe we sense through the body because we actually create it through the body as we go along.

remember, humanity sees everything backwards, and that is because of "me". "me" is the ego, and everything that "I" does seems to happen to "me" so "me" naturally assumes that what it experiences is happening to it, rather than a result of the creative nature of the "I" side of its own nature. i and me are two sides of the same coin, but because me sees with the senses it naturally experiences everything as happening to it and not to it happening to what it sees with those very senses. "I' happens and "me" experiences that happening as happening to it rather than because of it. "me" is the effect of the cause that is "I", but due to the nature of the senses inverts the natural cause and effect relationship and sees everything from a completely backwards perspective. effect becomes the totality of human experience, and cause is assigned to a god that “me” believes to be a separate being that is the cause of everything that happens to "me" rather than the indwelling presence of "I AM THAT I AM".

that is why the other side of moses talks with god, the ten commandments, are so completely misunderstood by mankind. they are not, as ted koppel once said "the ten suggestions", not rules that you have some choice regarding their application; but they are commandments, the laws of being. one cannot break the laws of being one can only believe them to be broken. "THOU SHALT NOT" truly must be understood as "THOU CANST NOT" to get this fully. while the body can be murdered, the soul cannot be killed because it is eternal, and so forth with all of the commandments. because there is only god, you can have no other god but god, though you can believe otherwise. why is that? because of the nature of god. god is life, god is love, and god is liberty. even god cannot break these laws as they are the very nature of god's being. if god could break his own rules, there would be no god, and therefore no universe. effect cannot exist without cause, and since god cannot defy god, neither can god's creation.

the eight commandment really expresses the deep truth of this by saying "thou shalt not take the lord thy god's name in vain, for he shall not find him guiltless who taketh his name in vain." which means "you cannot take the name of god (I AM) in vain, and to try to do that will exact consequences from which you cannot escape unless you stop trying to do that. notice that it says, "not find him guiltless" and not "will find him guilty" and you can see that even god is powerless to stop human beings from doing stupid things to themselves due to their ignorance, regardless of any "reasons" human beings have for justifying those stupid things. to say, "i feel sick" is to say, "i am sick" and regardless of the fact that saying it comes from feeling the symptoms, the name cannot be taken in vain, and the consequences cannot be avoided; unless one changes the thought that begins the process. the thought? the belief in illness. it is the belief in illness that opens the door for the first symptom to appear, that first sneeze or sniffle, that then leads the mind to consider the notion of "i am sick" and then begin to follow the process of determining what is "wrong" rather than realize that what is wrong is the very notion that "I" can be sick.

what this means, and this is the tough one for human beings to allow at all, let alone accept, is that all experience is chosen. that the choice is made without conscious awareness, without the consent of "me" is irrelevant to the choice itself, because that is the essence of liberty; the power to choose. when one has an experience such as the death of a child, especially a horrific one such as murder, the notion that there is a choice involved in the experience is so foreign that it is not even considered, but that does not change what is true; experience is chosen. knowing this truth did not make dealing with my daughter's murder easier to deal with, it made it harder. i had to reconcile the ideas of a loving, life giving, and liberty providing god with the horror of actually experiencing what i experienced when i found my daughter's body. my unwillingness to allow the truth of being did not change the truth of being one bit, but it did cause me to spend thirteen years reconciling that truth with my actual experience.

the simple fact is that i have no way to know why my daughter would choose the way her life ended, any more than i can know why the man who took that life did that. i had to allow the truth while i trudged through the hell of my thoughts and my emotions to reach the understanding of that truth. i did not walk her path any more than i walked his path, so i cannot know the "why's" they held for their choices. that tiny bit of allowance of the truth then opened the tiniest bit of the willingness to be wrong that allowed everything to fall into place. my daughter was not, is not, and never will be that body i found by that dumpster. my daughter is eternal, just as god is eternal, no beginning and no ending. this life is just a short stop in that realm of the eternal that is beyond human capacity to understand. even the universe, which had a beginning, will have an ending. the creator of the universe, and all of the individual expressions of that creator are not the universe but are the cause of that universe. the universe and all that it contains are the effect of that cause, and are therefore subject to the same thing, a beginning, and an ending.

the singularity that became the big bang was the idea of consciousness, of cause, seeking expression, seeking effect. the question to ask that leads to this understanding is utterly simple; "where did it bang?" that question cannot be answered directly in human terms because human terms are all about effect, not cause, as there are no words for cause. words themselves are the effect, thought/emotion are the cause. thought and emotion are the two sides of the coin that represent being, the universe and in human terms, the body, are the effect. the more intensely thoughts and emotions are attached to things physical, the more difficult it becomes to see beyond the physical and know that which dwells within the physical. once that tiny crack appeared in the attachment that i had to my daughter as a physical being, it exploded into the realization of the truth of her being that shattered the hold grief had on me and began to break down the wall that kept me from knowing her presence in my heart and my mind. i still miss the physical, but that is only memories which i will never lose. what i now have is eternal, her presence in my own. she lives in me.

that is pretty much it for now. believe me when i tell you that is only a beginning. as many words as you just read, they are just the introduction the this tell. to give you some understanding of the power that drives these tells, and especially this one; this took four hours to write. that includes breaks for coffee, cigarettes, bathroom, and simply moving about to restore circulation and flexibility. i typed this into a sticky note, and now i will copy and paste this into a word file to run the check for spelling, punctuation, and grammar. once that is done i will copy it back to the sticky note and also save the word file and a pdf file. it will not be otherwise edited, and i will not actually know its content until i read that pdf file. i am not concerned for the content as i know from where it comes,  and i have absolute trust in that source. it is perfect as god is perfect, and god is the author, not me. me has been listening to "in the hands of god" by the newsboys the entire time that "I" have been staying out of god's way, while providing this body for him to do the work. believe that or do not believe that. that is not relevant to me, only to your willingness to allow it for yourself.
