text:
1/3
RUSSIA–UKRAINE, 1991–2026: CAN PUTIN END THE WAR JUST BY DECLARING A CEASEFIRE? THE LAW, THE 1990s, KOSOVO AND THE OLDER SECURITY SYSTEM

Research cutoff: October 12, 2026.
Trigger: https://t.co/6oVjYCVRbL

Former U.S. ambassador Michael McFaul wrote: “Putin could end the war in Ukraine today by announcing a ceasefire. Zelenskyy would endorse a ceasefire immediately. It is not Zelensky's fault that this war continues. It is Putin's fault.” The essential issues are initiation, responsibility, a ceasefire's mechanics, and WHY the conflict did not begin in February 2022. No analysis should turn it into a secret Western plot, or pretend that twenty-five years of Russian security policy were invented personally by one man. (i)
THE IMMEDIATE FACT-CHECK:

Russia initiated the FEBRUARY 24, 2022 full-scale invasion of internationally recognized Ukrainian territory. The UN General Assembly, by 141 votes to five in March 2022, demanded Russia end its aggression and withdraw unconditionally. The International Court of Justice ordered Moscow to suspend military operations in a binding provisional-measures order. The ICJ order was NOT a final judgment resolving all legal disputes or a criminal conviction of Putin. (ii–iii)

Putin can order Russian regular forces to STOP offensive operations and attacks. That would be an enormously consequential unilateral act. But a public announcement is not a verified bilateral ceasefire, and a ceasefire is not automatically a peace treaty, withdrawal, recognition of Ukrainian sovereignty, release of prisoners, return of deported children, or a settlement of occupied territory. Russian command structures, proxies and allied forces must actually comply; reciprocal arrangements need monitoring. Saying a ceasefire announcement would instantly “end the war” collapses those distinct steps.

Kyiv has PUBLICLY accepted ceasefire proposals. On March 11, 2025, Ukraine and the U.S. jointly stated Kyiv's readiness for an immediate interim 30-day ceasefire, SUBJECT to Russian acceptance and simultaneous implementation. Ukraine also accepted the principle of a reciprocal halt to strikes against energy infrastructure. This substantially supports McFaul's assertion that Zelenskyy is prepared to cease fire—but not that he would approve any condition whatsoever. (iv)

RIGHT NOW: Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” on October 11, 2026. Kyiv reported that it learned about the proposal from the media; Zelenskyy said Ukraine would reciprocate an actual Russian halt. Russian strikes against Ukrainian energy facilities continued after the announcement, according to Ukraine and AP's October 12 reporting. Neither Moscow's enforceable consent nor a functioning monitored ceasefire has been independently established. A partial energy truce is not a general military ceasefire. (v)

Responsibility is ASYMMETRIC but not simplistic. The state that crosses another state's border and occupies its land bears a foundational responsibility for the resulting war. Governments also make consequential decisions AFTER invasion: Ukraine has attacked Russian military/logistical targets and oil refineries, has conducted cross-border operations, and can be accountable for any unlawful acts. Negotiation positions on all sides affect prospects for settlement. They do not retroactively transfer responsibility for launching Russia's invasion to the country defending itself.

FIRST, THE SECURITY CONTRACTS RUSSIA ITSELF SIGNED.

The 1975 Helsinki Final Act recognizes sovereign equality, territorial integrity, inviolability of European frontiers, peaceful alteration of borders by agreement, and a state's right to choose or decline alliances. These principles exist TOGETHER: Russia's security concerns do not erase Ukraine's sovereignty, while Ukraine's sovereign rights do not make Russian security fears imaginary. (vi)

Ukraine became independent after the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991; the vote for independence included majorities even in regions with substantial Russian-speaking populations. In 1994 Ukraine agreed to relinquish nuclear weapons stationed on its territory through the post-Soviet disarmament process. Under the BUDAPEST MEMORANDUM, Russia, the U.S. and U.K. reaffirmed respect for Ukraine's independence and borders and pledged to refrain from force and economic coercion. It offered security ASSURANCES, not an automatic NATO-style obligation to fight Russia for Ukraine. (vii)

In 1997 Boris Yeltsin's Russia signed a bilateral FRIENDSHIP TREATY with Ukraine, reiterating respect for territorial integrity and existing borders. Also in 1997, NATO and Russia's FOUNDING ACT endorsed sovereignty, non-use of force and states' rights to choose their security arrangements. These are vital facts: complaints about NATO do not erase instruments Moscow voluntarily accepted. (viii–ix)

BUT THE WESTERN SECURITY STORY IS NOT INVENTED EITHER.

Declassified 1990 diplomacy shows Western officials, including U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, offered Soviet leaders verbal assurances in the context of German reunification that NATO jurisdiction would not move “one inch” eastward. Precisely WHAT these statements covered, how long they endured, and whether later alliance enlargement violated their political spirit remain disputed among historians. The assurances were not a ratified blanket treaty permanently forbidding Eastern European countries from joining NATO. NATO expanded in 1999 and 2004, partly because states formerly dominated by Moscow actively sought protection. Russia perceived encroachment; Poland, the Baltic states and others perceived historical vulnerability to Russia. BOTH concerns influenced policy, but concern alone is not legal authority to annex a neighbor. (x)

SECOND, THIS GOES BEYOND PUTIN: 1992–1999.

MOLDOVA/TRANSNISTRIA, 1992: After Soviet disintegration, Moscow's 14th Army was stationed in Moldova's separatist Transnistrian region. An OSCE analysis describes Russian troop involvement, armaments transfers to separatist formations, a ceasefire and a long, unresolved withdrawal dispute. This happened under YELTSIN, not Putin's presidency. It established a recurring problem: Russian forces could be simultaneously described as mediators, peacekeepers, security guarantors and parties with their own military leverage. Local communities' real fears and political choices must not be erased, either. (xi)

GEORGIA/ABKHAZIA/SOUTH OSSETIA, 1991–94: Conflicts began amid Georgian nationalism, competing Ossetian and Abkhaz self-determination claims, militia attacks, external support, ethnic cleansing and displacement. Russian-led peacekeeping structures followed ceasefires in South Ossetia in 1992 and Abkhazia in 1994. This was NOT a single uncomplicated invasion launched from Moscow. Local actors committed serious abuses, including mass displacement of ethnic Georgians. Russia gained enduring military and political leverage through its peacekeeper role and support to separatist authorities. This history matters to the far larger 2008 war. (xii)

CHECHNYA, 1994–96: Boris Yeltsin launched a devastating military intervention inside the Russian Federation. U.S. State Department investigators documented indiscriminate Russian force and major abuses, as well as crimes by Chechen fighters. An August 1996 ceasefire sharply reduced the fighting, but did NOT resolve Chechnya's status; war resumed in 1999, when Putin had risen to prime minister. Chechnya was a war inside Russia, not legally equivalent to invading sovereign Ukraine, but it demonstrates a state-security and military culture pre-dating Putin's presidency, with disastrous civilian consequences and an incomplete peace. (xiii)

KOSOVO, 1998–1999: Serbian/Yugoslav forces committed grave abuses and mass displacement of Kosovar Albanians; Kosovo Liberation Army forces also committed abuses. NATO conducted a 78-day air war over Yugoslavia WITHOUT a prior UN Security Council authorization for the bombing. NATO defended its action as necessary to stop a humanitarian catastrophe, while Russia opposed it as an assault on sovereignty. Human Rights Watch estimated roughly 500 civilian deaths from NATO bombing and criticized particular targeting decisions. Those deaths and legality concerns cannot be omitted merely because NATO countries conducted the strikes. Nor do they erase the mass crimes of Serbian forces. Russia's 1999 opposition to NATO's action, and its unexpected peacekeeper deployment toward Pristina, became enduring reference points in Moscow's view of Western double standards. (xiv)

In 2008 Kosovo declared independence; in 2010 the ICJ issued a NARROW advisory opinion that the declaration itself did not violate international law. It did NOT proclaim a general right to annex another country after foreign troops seize territory; it did not decide that every separatist referendum creates statehood, nor settle all recognition disputes. Russia invoked Kosovo as a comparison in Georgia and Crimea, but invoking a perceived Western precedent is not the same as satisfying international law. (xv)

EARLY CONCLUSION: There are THREE separate levels—why Russian elites developed grievances and coercive regional methods; which governments committed particular abuses or unlawful actions; and what verifiable settlement can stop today's bloodshed. Diplomatic history can explain fears and mistakes. It does not turn Ukraine into Russian property. Parts 2 and 3 examine Georgia 2008, Maidan, Crimea, Donbas, the full-scale war, the international financial network and a credible ceasefire.

🇺🇸🇷🇺 Trump's Russian diesel deal could be the first step toward something extraordinary: America abandoning its longstanding alliance with Europe in favor of closer ties with Moscow.

While such a dramatic reversal may seem unlikely under present circumstances, the economic and geopolitical incentives driving Washington are beginning to change.

The terms of the diesel agreement offers an early example of this shift.

Washington has authorized Russian diesel transactions until April 2027, easing sanctions originally designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine.

The immediate motivation is lowering fuel prices, but the decision also demonstrates how economic interests can begin to outweigh longstanding geopolitical commitments.

For decades, Europe was an indispensable economic and strategic partner for America. Today, its value proposition is becoming increasingly difficult to defend.

Once a dominant engine of global economic growth, mainland Europe now struggles with industrial decline, expensive energy, sluggish growth and mounting defense costs.

And unlike Russia, it lacks the enormous oil and gas reserves that could compensate for those weaknesses.

This changes the strategic calculation for Washington.

Supporting Ukraine means spending billions confronting Russia, while rebuilding economic relations with Moscow offers access to vast natural resources, potentially cheaper energy and opportunities for trade.

One relationship demands enormous financial commitments. The other increasingly promises economic returns.

And as America's strategic priorities shift toward Asia, maintaining Europe's security becomes an increasingly difficult expense to justify.

The consequences could extend far beyond energy markets.

A stronger Russia emerging from the Ukraine war, combined with continued conservative leadership in Washington, could accelerate America's withdrawal from European security commitments and eventually bring NATO's future into question.

A complete American break with Europe remains a distant prospect, but the incentives that once held the transatlantic alliance together are changing.

We're now looking at the prospect of America gradually replacing its alliance with Europe with a strategic partnership with Russia.

Former British Prime Minister Theresa May has offered a revealing account of her encounters with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, describing a Russian president who appeared emotionally detached and an American president whose approach to diplomacy has changed dramatically.

Speaking to The Independent, May recalled Putin's behaviour during G20 summits, where his refusal to engage with fellow leaders left a lasting impression.

“Once a KGB man, always a KGB man. Putin was a completely cold fish.” - Theresa May 🇬🇧

According to May, Putin would sit around the table with other world leaders without making eye contact, reinforcing her perception of him as a distant and difficult figure.

Her scepticism toward Moscow long predated Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. May acknowledged that she had consistently taken a hard line on Russia, particularly after the 2018 Salisbury poisoning. She also argued that Britain had failed to respond adequately to the killing of Alexander Litvinenko, an unresolved issue that continued to overshadow relations between London and Moscow.

But her reflections were not limited to the Kremlin.

Turning to Trump, May recalled their famously awkward public interactions, joking that she might be the only world leader whose hand he had held. More seriously, she suggested that Trump's four years outside the White House had given him time to reconsider his political objectives and the people he wanted around him.

She also described a fundamental change in how foreign leaders are received in Washington.

During her premiership, Oval Office appearances generally began with diplomatic pleasantries in front of journalists. Once the cameras departed, substantive negotiations could begin privately.

May believes that distinction has increasingly disappeared.

“Now it's a TV show, as we sadly saw with the way President Zelensky was treated.” - Theresa May 🇬🇧

Her remarks draw attention to two very different diplomatic experiences: Putin's apparent reluctance to engage personally with other leaders and Trump's increasingly public, confrontational approach to high-level meetings.

For May, who dealt directly with both presidents, the contrast offers a revealing perspective on how the conduct of international diplomacy has changed, and how Ukraine has found itself at the centre of those changes.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the morning of October 12, 1870, the bells of Lexington began to toll in the clear autumn air of the Shenandoah Valley, and the word that Robert E. Lee was dead moved outward from the little college town. He had died at half-past nine in the president’s house on the Washington College grounds, in the bed that had been carried into the dining room so the family could keep watch. He was sixty-three. Outside, the leaves were turning. Inside, the house that had once been a place of quiet order fell into the deeper quiet of loss.

The illness had begun two weeks earlier, on the evening of September 28. After a long day at his desk and a vestry meeting at Grace Episcopal Church while a storm beat against the windows, Lee came home late for tea. The family was already gathered. He rose at the head of the table to say grace, as he always did, and no sound came. He stood for a moment, then sank back into his chair. For most of the next fourteen days he spoke little or not at all. His wife sat with his hand in hers. On the morning of the twelfth he simply stopped breathing. The doctors would later write that the remote cause had been the long strain of the war’s final year and the hard years that followed—mental and physical fatigue that at last produced a congestion of the brain.

What he had carried, after Appomattox, was the presidency of Washington College. In the summer of 1865 the trustees of a small, nearly ruined institution in the mountains of Virginia had offered him the post. He accepted it not because it promised ease or prominence, but because he believed the young men of the South needed schooling more than they needed further resistance. He rode into Lexington on Traveller and took the oath on October 2. Over the next five years he enlarged the faculty, broadened the course of study beyond the old classical curriculum, brought a law school into the college, and helped establish an honor system that would outlast him. Enrollment rose from a few dozen students to more than four hundred. Donors responded to his name and his quiet appeals. He kept regular hours, knew many of the students by name, and rode Traveller through the streets of the town as he had once ridden him across the fields of Virginia.

The funeral was shaped by weather and circumstance. A great freshet had swept down the Maury River, carrying away bridges and a shipment of metallic coffins. Two neighborhood boys later found one of the coffins washed ashore. It was undamaged and only slightly short; it would serve. Mrs. Lee preferred that her husband rest in Lexington rather than in Hollywood Cemetery in Richmond. On the morning of October 15 the procession formed in front of the president’s house. Old soldiers in worn gray, VMI cadets, college students, and townspeople moved slowly through the streets. Behind the hearse walked Traveller, the saddle and bridle draped in crape. At the college chapel—the building Lee had insisted be raised early in his presidency—the body was lowered into a brick vault beneath the floor. The Reverend William N. Pendleton, who had commanded Lee’s artillery, read the Episcopal service. On the marble slab above the vault a simple inscription was cut: Robert Edward Lee, Born January 19, 1807, Died October 12, 1870.

In the days that followed, the South measured the loss. Memorial meetings were held. Men who had followed Lee through the campaigns of 1862 and 1864 stood in silence or wrote letters home that said little more than that he was gone. The college would soon add his name to Washington’s. The man who had refused lucrative offers that would have traded only on his fame had spent his last years teaching the rising generation and walking the campus paths. On that October morning the Valley lost its most famous resident, and the larger country lost a figure whose post-war conduct had already begun to shape how many Americans would remember the conflict he had led.

text:
Christ brings peace principally through His redemptive work of atonement, which removes the fundamental cause of enmity—human sin—and restores right relationship with God. This is then extended by the gift of the Holy Spirit and the formation of the Church as a reconciled community.

Reconciliation through the Cross
Sin places humanity in a state of hostility toward God (Romans 5:10; Ephesians 2:3). Christ, as the incarnate Son and true Mediator, assumes human nature and offers His life as a perfect sacrifice. By the blood of His Cross He “killed the hostility,” making peace through the forgiveness of sins and the justification of the sinner (Colossians 1:19–20; Romans 5:1, 9). The *Catechism of the Catholic Church* (2305) summarizes this precisely: “By the blood of his Cross, ‘in his own person he killed the hostility,’ he reconciled men with God… ‘He is our peace.’” The objective peace with God is therefore secured by Christ’s obedience unto death and is received by faith and the sacraments that apply the merits of His Passion.

 The Gift of Interior Peace
Having reconciled the believer to the Father, Christ communicates His own peace. In the upper room He declared, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give it to you” (John 14:27). This is not a psychological technique or the mere absence of disturbance; it is the fruit of the indwelling Holy Spirit, who produces the peace that “surpasses all understanding” and guards the heart and mind (Philippians 4:7; Galatians 5:22). The risen Christ continues to bestow this gift, most explicitly in the post-resurrection appearances (“Peace be with you,” John 20:19, 21, 26) and through the sacramental life of the Church.

 Horizontal Reconciliation and the Church
The same Cross that unites men to God also unites them to one another. Christ “has broken down the dividing wall of hostility” between Jew and Gentile, creating “one new humanity” in Himself (Ephesians 2:14–16). The Church is thereby constituted as the sacrament of unity, the visible community in which the peace of Christ is both received and extended. Earthly efforts at peace remain fragile unless they are ordered to this deeper reconciliation; they are, in the language of the Catechism, “the image and fruit of the peace of Christ.”

 Eschatological Fulfillment
The peace inaugurated by Christ’s first coming will be consummated at His return. Isaiah’s prophecy anticipates a government whose increase of peace will have no end (Isaiah 9:7). Until that day, believers experience the peace of Christ as a real but partial participation in the *shalom* of the coming Kingdom—already given, not yet fully realized.

In short, Christ brings peace by removing the barrier of sin through His sacrifice, by pouring out the Spirit who bestows interior peace, by gathering a reconciled people, and by promising the final establishment of an everlasting kingdom of justice and peace. All authentic Christian peace flows from and returns to this single redemptive center.

text:
Stoicism and the (Aspirer Firm) Inner Temple Framework aren’t the same system, but they share some meaningful connections.

Here’s where they meet:

• Both view thoughts as interpretations rather than automatic truths.
• Both encourage a pause between stimulus and response.
• Both recognize that feelings don’t have to drive decisions.
• Both support a steadier inner life, especially under pressure.

Where they differ:

• Stoicism offers a complete philosophy of the good life, with virtue as its goal.
• The Inner Temple is a coaching framework for high achievers, bringing together pillars and CBT/REBT tools.
• Stoicism focuses on what is “up to you.”
• The Inner Temple also offers a structured way to work with the body, relationships, and patterns of tying your worth to performance.

How clients can use both:

• Stoic question: “Is this in my control?”
• Inner Temple question: “Which pillar is under strain?”
• Shared practice: Notice the thought, test it, and choose an action guided by your values.

You don’t have to become a Stoic to benefit from the pause, and you don’t have to set aside clinical tools to honor ancient wisdom.

Feel it. Name what’s yours to do. Then decide from principle, rather than at the peak of the emotion.

Aspire Higher. Build Firmer.

Marie Cook, LPC
Founder, Aspirer Firm

But the mycelium never died.

You cannot easily destroy a living network by severing a single thread.

Break one connection, and under the right conditions, the network can grow again along another path.

And what if this offers us a metaphor for the survival of ancient knowledge?

Across generations, traditions have endured through:

— Yajna rituals that preserve specific choices of sacred wood
— Abhisheka ceremonies involving traditional offerings
— Sufi whirling and other contemplative practices
— Amazonian Ayahuasca traditions
— Lakota and other Indigenous peyote ceremonies
— Local temple traditions whose meanings have been passed down through generations

These practices are distinct, rooted in different histories and worldviews. Their survival does not prove they all descend from one ancient mushroom tradition.

But the image of the mycelium remains powerful.

Knowledge can be interrupted.
Traditions can be transformed.
Memories can disappear—and return in unexpected forms.

Perhaps the network was never one secret ritual, but humanity's enduring search for the sacred.

The “indigenous” framing is frequently a modern political construct applied selectively, and 19th–early 20th-century Arab in-migration into the sparsely populated Ottoman districts that became Mandate Palestine is well-documented (economic pull from Jewish development + better administration). Continuous Jewish presence, archaeology, language, religion, and legal ties to the land go back millennia and are not comparable to 18th/19th-century settlement waves. Treating one as “pseudoscience” while treating the other as self-evident is special pleading.
“Hamas has no necessity” is correct in the abstract. It is the product of specific choices: rejection of every partition plan that offered Arab self-rule, the 1948 war of annihilation, the PLO/Hamas charters and educational materials that define the conflict as existential until Jewish sovereignty ends, and the post-2005 Gaza experiment of self-rule that produced rockets, tunnels, and Oct 7 rather than state-building. Gazans are not unique in human history for being unable or unwilling to relocate en masse; the difference is that UNRWA and regional politics have actively preserved refugee status for generations while Jewish refugees from Arab countries were absorbed. Neighboring Arab states have large territories and populations; the refusal to integrate or resettle is political, not geographic destiny.
Attachment to a place is normal human behavior, not a “spiritual myth” invented by social media. People fight for homes, graves, and continuity everywhere (see Kurds, Armenians, Tibetans, etc.). The relevant distinction is between a people with an ancient, continuous civilizational link who accepted partition and a national movement that has repeatedly prioritized eliminating the other side over building its own polity. Dismissing the former as aesthetics while treating the latter’s maximalist claims as natural is not chronology—it’s preference.
If the actual goal is dismantling exclusive territorial nationalism in favor of civic arrangements, that standard has to apply symmetrically. Otherwise it is just selective pressure on one side.

text:
These are great insights, but what ARE MXenes?    I attended the Advanced Materials Show in Pittsburgh last week and sat in on a MXene presentation.  

MXenes are transition metal carbides and nitrides.  These are compounds made from a transition metal like titanium, vanadium, niobium, molybdenum, tantalum, etc., combined with carbon (carbides) or nitrogen (nitrides).

In these 3D materials, the small carbon or nitrogen atoms sit in the spaces between the larger metal atoms. This creates strong bonding that mixes metallic, covalent, and some ionic character.

Bulk (3D) versions are well-known hard materials:

•  Extremely hard and wear-resistant, used in cutting tools, drill bits, coatings, and tungsten carbide jewelry

•  Very high melting points

•  Good electrical conductivity

•  Examples: titanium carbide (TiC), tungsten carbide (WC), titanium nitride (TiN)

MXenes

MXenes are the two-dimensional, atomically thin versions of these materials. They come from layered precursors called MAX phases (M = transition metal, A = typically aluminum or similar, X = carbon and/or nitrogen).

The process is:
1.  Start with a MAX phase (e.g., Ti₃AlC₂)

2.  Selectively etch out the “A” layer (usually aluminum)

3.  What remains are thin sheets of transition metal carbide/nitride, usually with surface groups (–O, –OH, –F, etc.) attached

Conventional MXene production involves fluorides and carries clear safety, environmental, and materials-performance drawbacks. The field is actively moving toward fluoride-free methods to address them, but these methods are lower-yielding. 

Uses of MXenes

•  Metallic conductivity combined with hydrophilic (water-loving) surfaces

•  High surface area and tunable chemistry

•  Especially interesting for energy storage (batteries, supercapacitors), EMI shielding, sensors, and catalysis

Why I Am Focused on Graphene

MXenes remain earlier-stage, and production is still only at pilot quantities of kilograms, not tonnes.  The absolute market remains small through the early 2030s.  Production is harder to scale consistently.

Graphene offers the more probable near-to-medium-term returns with broader application diversity and scaling capabilities. 

Hydrograph is the most advanced commercial story today in the pure graphene space, based on their quality, consistency, and their clean, efficient production methods that are scalable.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the morning of October 12, 1892, in schoolrooms from New England to the Pacific, children stood at their desks while teachers unfurled American flags that, in many places, had never before hung on the wall. The occasion was the 400th anniversary of Columbus’s landfall, and across the country the day had been declared a national holiday.

The words the children were about to speak had been written only weeks earlier by a young Baptist minister named Francis Bellamy. Working for *The Youth's Companion*, a popular family magazine, Bellamy had been enlisted in a campaign to place a flag in every public school and to give the rising generation a common expression of loyalty. His brief text was meant to be learned in a single recitation: “I pledge allegiance to my Flag and the Republic for which it stands, one nation, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.” The phrase “under God” was not yet part of it; that addition would wait more than sixty years.

Bellamy himself was present in spirit if not in every classroom. He had drafted the pledge as the centerpiece of a carefully staged national exercise. On that Columbus Day morning, teachers were instructed to lead the children in a short program that included the reading of a proclamation, a few songs, and then the new pledge, delivered with the right arm extended stiffly toward the flag in the gesture later known as the Bellamy Salute. In rooms still heated by woodstoves, with the smell of chalk and damp wool coats hanging in the air, thousands of young voices rose together for the first time.

The moment was both ceremonial and practical. Barely a generation after the Civil War, the country was absorbing millions of new immigrants while still nursing old sectional wounds. The pledge offered a short, portable ritual that could be taught to children whose parents spoke different languages and whose grandparents had fought on opposite sides. It was civic catechism in the simplest possible form—flag, republic, indivisible nation, liberty and justice—spoken in unison so that the act of saying the words became, for a few seconds, the thing itself.

The children finished the pledge, lowered their arms, and returned to their seats. Few of them could have imagined that the short sentence they had just spoken would outlast the century and nearly every other public ritual of their time.

What began that morning as a magazine-sponsored exercise became, almost overnight, a national habit. The wording would be revised, the salute discarded, and “under God” inserted under Eisenhower, yet the essential scene—children standing together beneath an American flag—remained. On October 12, 1892, the Republic asked its youngest citizens to declare their allegiance out loud, and, in classrooms across the land, they did.

We must recognize that this era is one of a "war of words," a war of narratives. The long-familiar "word magic" continues unabated.

Yet, it must finally be stated: democracy itself—"representative democracy," that mere "game of voting"—is the flawed system.

On one side, the importance of "democratic principles" is emphasized ad nauseam, while the other side couldn't care less about the "democratic values" it once held up as a shield.

A few days ago, I watched a discussion. It was about culture. The visionary once responsible for cultural funding still fails to grasp that, by applying a fabricated principle, *they* were the very ones who unleashed this satanic demon upon the nation.

No, it is not guilt he lacks—it is an understanding of the situation itself: that an enemy devoid of any moral principles has set its sights on our annihilation.
For if everything is destroyed, the mountains of our corpses will conceal their sins and blunders.

The first step is to throw the rotting pear out of the basket. You will see: *that* is the one! The brown, spotted, stinking one. It matters not that it keeps repeating, "I came from among you; I am a pear, too."

You stink, my dear fellow!  You are no longer a pear... but some kind of scumbag...

Forget it; pay no heed when he keeps repeating: "I am a Piarist student."

So what? Luther and Calvin went to Benedictine schools... So what?

But he shook hands with the Pope...
So what?
Kádár did that too. In fact, perhaps Brezhnev did as well. [No, he didn't.]

We must state clearly that an enemy acting like an enemy is—the ENEMY. Once you say this, the moral shackles that had been holding us back fall away, and you become capable of defending yourself and defeating the one bent on your destruction.

And cast out from your ranks anyone who parrots liberal principles! It is a dead end. It offers no solution—if only because your enemy has used those very principles solely to deceive and weaken you.

Liberalism is a false doctrine.
Modernism is a false doctrine.
Just as Protestantism—always rebelling against all authority (yet somehow always silent when facing the *real* enemy)—is also a false doctrine.

One must not support, serve, or kowtow to the filth of liberalism.

You saw the funding amounts given to the traitorous liberal scum we supported... Those were huge sums of money.
The Bródys, the Noárs, the Gesztis—that urban rabble poisoning Hungary intellectually. In the name of a "principle," we fed our enemies.  True, they were fed by the "non-existent" shadow power—by Satan himself, hiding behind the masks of various secret services—and we fed them too.
Double the profit.

What forced you into this?
Their false "principles"—principles you adopted and adhered to, while they did not.

Wake up, Hungary!
There is a war on!
Yet you keep telling yourself: "there is no war, there is no war, there is no war!"
The enemy is at the gates.
The gate has been breached.
The swarming rabble will show no respect for the Hagia Sophia where you have taken refuge.
Did you not know? Yet history is the teacher of life.

The island is sinking. And still, you lie to yourself: we are not sinking.

The most dangerous moment for a democracy is not when power begins to turn authoritarian. It comes when the very institutions created to restrain that power start functioning as its instruments.

That is the most serious question facing India today.

The allegation against the Narendra Modi government is not merely one of abusing power. The far more serious charge is that the independence and impartiality of the institutions created to protect democracy are themselves at stake.

Look at the recent events in Delhi. Images have emerged of people threatening protesters with sticks, followed by the same people’s car being escorted out through a police security cordon. Journalists kept demanding an investigation, but the police cleared the way for the car to pass.

And amid all this, the Chief Justice of India says that law and order related to protests is not their responsibility.

Of course, law and order is the responsibility of the police. But when the police themselves are accused of crushing citizens’ constitutional rights and protecting violent elements, where does the judiciary’s responsibility begin?

The Election Commission’s impartiality is under scrutiny. Serious allegations have been raised about the role of the police. Concerns over the autonomy of constitutional institutions are deepening by the day.

A picture is emerging in which citizens who disagree with the government are being targeted, while the institutions meant to restrain and question those in power appear to be abandoning their constitutional role and becoming instruments of the government.

That is why the allegation is so serious that the government has turned constitutional institutions into its ‘sharp shooters’ while behaving like a mafia gang itself.

The mafia’s method is simple. intimidate opponents, protect your own people, and use the law according to your convenience.

But democracy is not the property of any gang. The Constitution is not the private possession of any prime minister. And the institutions of the state are not a loyal army of any political party.

History offers a brutal lesson. When a government becomes so blinded by arrogance that it begins to see the Constitution, the people and the independence of institutions as obstacles in its path, it is preparing the ground for its own downfall.

And look at the irony,

The authoritarianism that makes such a government believe itself invincible can one day generate such public anger that it may erupt with such force that not even a trace of its name remains in the corridors of power.

Because history has never seen a government become powerful enough to keep both the people and time under its control forever.

5th State Level Archery Championship 2026 Concludes in Tawang; Indian Army Announces Initiative to Nurture Young Archery Talent
Tawang, October 12, 2026: The closing ceremony of the 5th State Level Archery Championship 2026 was held at the Gyalwa Tsangyang Gyatso High Altitude Sports Stadium, Tawang, with Lieutenant General Neeraj Shukla, AVSM, SM, General Officer Commanding (GOC), 4 Corps, gracing the occasion as the Chief Guest. Leki Gombu, Zilla Parishad Chairperson (ZPC), attended as the Guest of Honour.
The ceremony was attended by Major General Amit Nautiyal, SM, VSM, GOC, 5 Mountain Division; Brigadier Vimal Tikoo, Commander, Tawang Brigade; Tenzin Monpa, ZPM Kyidphel; Sonam Nordzin, ZPM Tawang; Thutan Gombu, ZPM Lungla; Tasi Darang, Superintendent of Police, Tawang; senior district administration officials; and representatives of the Arunachal Pradesh and Tawang Archery Associations. MLA Tawang Namgey Tsering also attended the award distribution ceremony in the afternoon.
Indian Army Announces Initiative to Nurture Young Archery Talent
A major highlight of the closing ceremony was the inspiring announcement by Lieutenant General Neeraj Shukla regarding the Indian Army's initiative to identify and nurture talented young archers from Arunachal Pradesh.
He announced that willing and deserving young archers identified through the championship would be provided opportunities for advanced training at the Army Sports Institute, Pune. During the training period, the Indian Army would take care of their education, food and accommodation. He further stated that under the proposed initiative, those who attain 18 years of age and wish to join the Army would be considered for direct recruitment.

Highlighting the Indian Army's commitment to sporting excellence, he stated that the Army was working towards nurturing young talent across six sporting disciplines and preparing promising athletes for upcoming national and international competitions in mission mode. The initiative is expected to open new avenues for aspiring sportspersons from Arunachal Pradesh, enabling them to pursue excellence in sports while building a secure and promising future.

text:
My work van vanished in broad daylight.

I left it outside a hardware store in Phoenix while I ran in to grab a few supplies.

I wasn't inside for more than fifteen minutes.

When I came back, the space was empty.

At first I thought I'd parked in the wrong row.

I walked the entire lot twice before reality finally hit me.

Someone had stolen my van.

Inside were thousands of dollars' worth of tools I'd spent years collecting.

The police took my report, but they were realistic.

"Most stolen vehicles are either stripped for parts or used in other crimes," the officer told me.

I drove home feeling sick.

There was one detail I remembered later that evening.

Months earlier, I'd installed a hidden GPS tracker under the dashboard after a friend's truck was stolen.

I opened the app.

Nothing.

The tracker had gone offline.

Five days passed without a single update.

Then, just after midnight, my phone buzzed.

The signal was back.

The van was no longer in Arizona.

It was sitting outside an abandoned warehouse in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

I called the local police immediately and shared the location.

They said officers would check it out, but couldn't tell me when.

Every hour felt endless.

Against everyone's advice, my cousin Marcus offered to drive with me the next morning.

We agreed we wouldn't confront anyone we only wanted to see if the van was really there.

From across the street, we spotted it.

The paint had been spray painted black.

The license plates were different.

It looked like someone had tried to erase its identity overnight.

As we watched, two men walked out of the warehouse, loaded several large boxes into the back, then disappeared inside again.

We stayed hidden and called 911.

Within minutes, multiple police vehicles surrounded the building.

The suspects tried to escape through a side entrance but were caught before they made it far.

Feature 4: He showed him Cabin Overheat Protection  the safety feature most owners don’t know runs after they park.

He told him about the feature that protects the car’s interior  and any living thing accidentally left inside  from dangerous heat buildup.

Cabin Overheat Protection  enabled in Controls → Safety → Cabin Overheat Protection  activates automatically after the car is parked and the owner leaves. When the interior temperature reaches approximately 105°F (40°C), the car activates the climate system to reduce the temperature  even with no one inside and no keys present. The system runs for up to 12 hours after the car was last driven.

He told him the feature has 3 modes. “On”  the air conditioning runs to cool the cabin. “Fan Only”  the fan circulates air without running the A/C (uses less battery). “Off”  no protection. The A/C mode provides the strongest cooling but uses more battery. The fan-only mode provides moderate cooling with minimal battery consumption.

He told him Cabin Overheat Protection does 2 things most owners don’t consider. It protects the interior  dashboard, touchscreen, leather seats, and electronics  from the extreme heat that damages materials over years of sun exposure. The dashboard that cracks after 5 years in Arizona cracks because Cabin Overheat Protection was never enabled. It also provides a safety margin for the nightmare scenario  a child, a pet, or a person accidentally left in a parked car. The system isn’t designed as a child-safety feature (and should never replace attentive supervision), but the automatic cooling that activates at 105°F provides a protective layer that no other consumer vehicle offers by default.

text:
Columbus Day

Across the unknown waters,
driven by more than wind,
a sailor fixed his course
on a hope he could not see.

Three ships against the dark,
sails taut with purpose,
men who prayed and watched
the stars that never moved.

They carried more than compasses—
they carried the cross,
the word of a Father who commands
the seas and the hearts of men.

When land rose from the deep,
it was not merely earth;
it was a threshold given,
a door the centuries had waited for.

From that first footprint
came a people who would learn
to order liberty under Heaven,
to build what none had built,
to guard what must be guarded.

We remember not only the man,
but the courage that sails
when the horizon offers no promise
except the promise kept by Our HeavenlyFather.

On this day we give thanks
for those who crossed the waters,
for the land they opened,
and for the faith that still calls
ordinary men to extraordinary seas.

Strength and Honor.

text:
What are we incentivizing when non-workers and people on public assistance get discounts on things like retail memberships, museums, and zoos, while people who work must pay full price?   If on public assistance and you have access to these luxury goods for a cheaper price why would you want to get a job and lose all of these perks?

Common examples provided by Grok: 

Retail and subscription services: Amazon Prime Access offers a discounted membership (around $6.99/month instead of the standard ~$14.99) to WIC participants. Walmart+ has a similar half-price option for WIC/EBT/Medicaid holders. Some grocery chains (e.g., certain Kroger Boost memberships) offer reduced premium loyalty plans.⁠

Cultural and entertainment venues: Beyond Museums for All (which primarily uses SNAP EBT but many sites also accept WIC), state programs like Massachusetts’ WIC Card to Culture give free or heavily discounted admission/tickets at hundreds of museums, theaters, and arts organizations. Similar “passport” or partner programs exist in places like Virginia. Individual theaters (e.g., Guthrie Theater in Minnesota) offer low-cost tickets ($5 range) with proof of WIC or other benefits. Zoos and museums in many states explicitly list WIC discounts (e.g., $2–$12 per person or reduced memberships).⁠

Parks and recreation: Vermont Parks Forever provides free day-use entry to state parks for WIC (and other benefit) cardholders during the season, while others pay regular fees. Some YMCAs and gyms offer sliding-scale or reduced memberships based on WIC/SNAP eligibility.⁠

Internet and other services: Programs like Comcast Internet Essentials (and similar low-cost broadband options) are available to low-income households, including many WIC participants. Farmers markets often have separate WIC Farmers Market Nutrition Program vouchers for produce.

At that purchase range, $60k–$100k remains after assumed rehab, BEFORE transaction costs, financing, holding and profit.

Here’s how we’d move it through our network:

text:
Copied... it seems that many Bantu societies were organised along matrilineal lines, and were governed by women; a whole heap of oral legends testifies to this, and female founding ancestors - where they exist in tradition - are as venerated and respected as their male counterparts.

Being a settled culture, the Bantu were inherently at risk of attack from the mobile nomadic Nilotic and Cushitic cattle and camel herders such as the Maasai, Borana (Oromo) and Somali, and as a result many Bantu societies became characterised by their defensive nature. None of the Kenyan Bantu groups lived on open land (ideal territory for the herders), having preferred, for both economic (agricultural) and defensive reasons, to occupy the less accessible highland regions.
   Settlements were built with the greatest attention to defence, and were also well concealed: Europeans found they could be walking only metres from a settlement without knowing of its existence.
   Some tribes, like the Kikuyu, became experts at adapting and adopting to new realities, and rarely resorted to conflict. Others, like the Chuka, developed an array of inventive defensive measures, ranging from ingenious traps to tree houses and fortifications. Almost all the Bantu groups also adopted a rigid system of age-sets (an idea possibly borrowed from the Nilotic or Cushitic peoples they came across), in which all people of similar age were initiated into an age-set, which together progressed through clearly defined phases of social responsibilities, functions and status, from initiation, through warriorhood, marriage and elderhood to death.
   The system ensured the cohesion of society, as well as enabling the development of the warrior system, by which all the young men of a given society would, shortly after initiation to adulthood and their age-set, take up the role of defending the entire society.

For the Mijikenda in the coastal hills, the situation was similar. Having been pushed south by the Somali/Oromo expansion, they settled on hilltops which offered more protection against the nomadic herders than the lowlands. There they developed specific defensive settlements, called kaya, to protect people and property from raiders.

Nowadays, the Bantu reliance on agriculture and latterly trade has meant that they are by far the richest of Kenya's people, at least in monetary terms. The downside is that their settlements are inevitably densely populated, a problem which has grown acute over the last few decades.

text: I have taken a hard critical look at the projected  geography of the coastal road when it began at the loom. First, I recognised that coastal roads are not novel concepts developed in nigeria. We have coastal roads in the US, in Canada, in Chile, Europe, China, Ukraine and other places. Looking at the map of the projected Coastal road and the high cost of deliverables in Nigeria  today, coupled with the general nigerian penchant for corruption, and the dilapidated state of existing roads infrastructure in the areas a new coastal roads were to pass like the Edo Delta, East West roads corridor, I had argued that an additional coastal road while it could overburden  scarce resources will not answer the question of the much needed sustainability of existing roads network  in the area. I wrote a 15 part thesis why the government must reconsider  its stand on the coastal roads architecture. I am not an architect but try to do  an unconventional mapping of road infrastructure that could include Ajebamidele Ipaye from the Ogun corridor  and from there through existing road network to Edo state that would further take the road through Delta state to link the East West roads and from there to Itam in Akwa Ibom  and then to Calabar. I had said in my paper that while this arrangement could salvage existing roads infrastructures, it would reduce cost and offer the government more  time to gather resources to adjoin the remaining outlying areas of the original coastal road map. I am happy this government  acknowledged my paper and is addressing  the concerns raised.

Cinematic photoreal fantasy comedy, warm golden-hour light in a village stone bakery yard: a big stone brick oven with an open arched mouth, wooden table, bowl of flour, clay pots, barrels, firewood stack, soft god rays, shallow depth of field, rich warm grade. @Image1 is the Girl (rolled sleeves, laced dark bodice vest, brown skirt), expressive. @Image2 is the Dragon (pearl-white, pink spikes, amber eyes, about 10 times bigger than the Girl, gentle and playful). No watermark, no text, no logos.

SHOT 1 (0:00-0:01.7) — Dough into the Oven
• Medium shot: the Dragon's huge head on the left, nostrils glowing red. The Girl smiles and slides a round white dough on a long wooden paddle into the big stone oven, then points at the oven opening and at the Dragon. GIRL (cheerful, English): "Okay, chef, breathe your fire into the oven for me!"

SHOT 2 (0:01.7-0:03) — Full Fire
• EFFECT: Speed ramp into slow-motion (about 30%)
• Low-angle close-up: the Dragon blows a huge flame into the oven, fire roars inside and bursts out of the oven mouth, sparks fly. The Girl's face freezes in shock beside the oven.

SHOT 3 (0:03-0:05.8) — Burnt Bread
• Medium shot: the Girl pulls the dough out with the paddle: it is a black burnt lump with glowing embers. She gasps in shock, then flicks the burnt loaf off the paddle, it spins through the air. GIRL (shocked, loud, English): "Oh no! You used too much fire!"

SHOT 4 (0:05.8-0:07.3) — Sorry Dragon
• ECU of the Dragon's amber eyes looking guilty, smoke curling from the oven behind. Cut to a medium two-shot: the Dragon ducks its head sheepishly while the Girl throws up her hands. GIRL (shouting, English): "You burned it! That's way too much fire!"

SHOT 5 (0:07.3-0:11.6) — New Dough Lesson
• Medium shot: the Girl kneads a fresh heart-shaped dough, places it on the paddle and slides it into the stone oven. The Dragon watches closely. She points at its mouth, then makes a tiny gesture with her fingers. GIRL (calm, teaching, English): "A little bit at a time. Breathe the fire gently through your mouth, so the bread bakes." The Dragon closes its eyes, concentrating hard.

SHOT 6 (0:11.6-0:13.3) — Gentle Flame
• EFFECT: Extreme close-up + rack focus
• ECU: the Dragon's nostrils glow softly, a tiny controlled flame flows into the oven mouth. Focus shifts from its eyes to the glowing oven interior.

SHOT 7 (0:13.3-0:15.2) — Dough Rises
• EFFECT: Macro shot + slow-motion (about 40%)
• Macro inside the oven: the dough puffs up over the glowing coals, turns golden and becomes a crusty golden loaf. Heat shimmer, flour dust floating in the glow.

AUDIO: Girl's dialogue as marked, natural warm female voice. Dragon low rumble and inhale, loud whoomph on the full flame, roaring oven fire, wooden paddle scrape, gentle flame hiss, light playful folk music.
Same style, same lighting, same characters, same bakery yard. @Image1 is the Girl, @Image2 is the Dragon. No watermark, no text, no logos.

SHOT 8 (0:15.2-0:16.4) — Shock
• ECU: the Girl's wide eyes and open mouth, firelight on her face. GIRL (amazed, English): "Wow... look at that!"

SHOT 9 (0:16.4-0:19) — Joy
• Medium shot: the Dragon's tiny flame still glows on the golden loaf, the Girl's face lights up and she claps her hands excitedly. GIRL (happy, English): "Yes! That's exactly how you do it!"

SHOT 10 (0:19-0:23) — Cut and Taste
• Medium shot: the Girl cuts the loaf with a knife, steam rises from the soft inside, she tears a piece, tastes it, closes her eyes in delight. The Dragon watches, head tilting, its tail swishing behind. She laughs and pats its snout. GIRL (delighted, English): "Mmm... you baked this so well!"

SHOT 11 (0:23-0:26.5) — Basket of Heart Rolls
• Medium shot: the table now holds a basket of heart-shaped bread rolls. The Girl lifts the basket and offers a roll, smiling up at the Dragon. GIRL (warm, English): "Here, you try one too!" The Dragon leans in gently.
• EFFECT: Slow pull-back
• Wide shot: the Dragon lies with its head down and eyes closed, content, small smoke puffs from its nose. The Girl stands next to the stone oven with the basket, fire flickering, golden dust in the air. Camera slowly pulls back and holds.

AUDIO: Girl's dialogue as marked, warm and happy. Gentle fire crackle, knife cutting crust, bread crackle, soft chew sounds, dragon purr and deep happy breath, warm cozy folk music building and fading at the end.

text:
‼️ California metallurgist David Xu, who pleaded no contest to poisoning a colleague Rong Yuan, is seeking to have his felony conviction dismissed, years after hidden-camera footage exposed him contaminating her water bottle with toxic heavy metal cadmium ‼️

David Xu, a metallurgist at Berkeley Engineering and Research, spiked his colleague Rong Yuan’s food and water with cadmium — a toxic heavy metal — for nearly 18 months between 2017 and 2019. As Yuan suffered debilitating symptoms, hospital visits and fear of a terminal illness, Xu maintained a deceitful facade, even suggesting her illness was caused by “mold” in the office.

His poisoning campaign only unraveled in early 2019 when Yuan set up a hidden camera at her desk, capturing Xu in the act of tampering with her water bottle.

The video evidence led to Xu’s arrest in Mar 2019 on charges of attempted murder and poisoning, which also affected Yuan’s parents, who had inadvertently consumed the poisoned water.

Xu faced up to life in state prison.

After his arrest, Xu was released on $2 million bail. He then received repeated modifications to his home confinement, with his travel restrictions eventually fully lifted,

A judge set bail at $2 million, and Xu was released on GPS monitoring. In April, Attorney General Xavier Becerra filed a motion on behalf of the state engineering board, calling Xu “a highly trained and unusually sophisticated criminal defendant” who “used a number of chemicals in his work.” A judge agreed with the AG’s order and barred Xu from practicing under his state engineering licenses during the case.

In the ensuing months, the court granted Xu more and more leniency. By July, he was allowed 6 hours out of the house each week to take his daughter to ballet and gymnastics classes. In Oct, he received 6 more hours out of the house on Sundays. In June 2021, he was granted “an additional day with kids.” By Sep, he was allowed an additional 2 hours every day of the week. In Nov, his request to end house arrest was granted. By Apr 2022, he was allowed to travel within the U.S.

In Sep 2023, Xu pleaded no contest to a single count of poisoning under a deal offered by prosecutors under Alameda County district attorney Pamela Price, with one year of felony probation and one day of credit for time served. A no-contest plea carries the same weight as a conviction but is not an admission of the underlying facts.

Yuan had sought nearly $500,000 in restitution. A judge ordered her paid $7,058, citing a report Xu’s attorney had submitted by a toxicologist who concluded that cadmium poisoning would not cause long-term health effects. 

Xu finished his two years of probation in March. On Oct 12, he will ask an Alameda County judge to dismiss his felony conviction — a process commonly referred to as “expungement.” Under state law, a person who completes every condition of probation is entitled to expungement, and California appeals courts have held that judges cannot deny those petitions unless the crime is on a short list of exclusions — poisoning not being one of them. A dismissal would not erase the case; Xu’s record would still show an arrest and conviction to law enforcement, and the conviction could be used against him if he is charged with a new crime. He would also have to disclose it on applications for state licenses.

text:
Let's talk about three ways to add an extra 100K in recurring income during the next 12 months. I think this is pretty timely. First, though, let me state the obvious. Owning a business or working for the man can be stressful at times, especially in this chaotic environment. However, when you have multiple streams of cash flow, it gives you a nice cushion and the ability to create your own economy. 

Here are the methods in no particular order:

1) Private coaching/consulting

This is an income source that I’ve been blessed in abundance with. It still blows my mind that people are willing to pay a premium for experience-based advice. I get it, though. It’s what I personally do in many areas of my life. If I need information that I know will grow my business, I seek out a master in that specific area. It’s much cheaper for me to buy speed from an expert than to mess around learning for weeks, months, or more. This is one reason the rich get richer. 

The top 1% always know the value of their time and are interested in speed of implementation. Time is money.

In my business, I offer private Zoom coaching, a weekly mastermind and an in-person total immersion day. Each of those programs require an application. I get to work with professionals I want to work with and they pay handsomely for my guidance.  

It turns out that those that pay high prices for a service value it more, are less hassle to me, implement what I say, get the best results and make the greatest case studies. It really doesn’t get any better than that.

2) Start doing speaking gigs

In 2006, my life changed forever in a few different ways. My name was getting around in different circles, and a network marketing company got a hold of me, wanting to speak to their company CEO about Myspace and YouTube marketing. I was kind of new to speaking at that time, and they asked me what my fee was to present for an hour. “Umm …,” I thought to myself. Then I just blurted out, “$1,500 plus airfare and accommodations.” 

The next thing that came out of this guy’s mouth was, “Can we meet this Tuesday in Houston?”

I was floored.

That’s when I got a taste of how lucrative speaking could be. I ended up flying there and speaking for around an hour and a half. I got home back in Atlanta around 5:00pm that day and sat in front of my computer for about an hour wondering what the heck just happened.

Since that time, I’ve performed countless speaking engagements, get paid honorariums, and I'm usually allowed to make an offer from stage after my talk. The acquisition of knowledge is VERY important in today’s time. It doesn’t matter what business you have. You have information and experience that others simply don’t. 

There’s absolutely no reason you can’t earn an extra $5,000 per month just from speaking. Not to mention that most of the time you get to offer your product or service when you’re finished, which leads to way more back-end sales and income.

3) Master information marketing

If you've followed me for any length of time you likely know how my secondary source of income became my primary, overtaking my practice. I accomplished this through profitable marketing of an online course. Actually, when it was first released it was on DVD's and came with a booklet. This training simply solved a huge problem that the market was facing.

Digital products can be sold 24/7, which enables you to break away from the “time for money” hamster wheel. Imagine having sales pour into your bank account while you sleep. It’s a total game changer and never gets old. 

I’m going to group affiliate marketing into this category as well since it’s where you take a product (physical or digital) that someone else has created and promote it. This is where I actually got my feet wet in Internet marketing in 2005.

The first affiliate commission I made changed my life. 
It opened my eyes to the fact that making real money online was not only possible, but it could be used to grow a six and seven-figure business. As I built email lists in different industries, the commissions came easier and faster!

As an affiliate, you don’t have to stock any inventory; there’s no recruiting others; there are no products to ship and no handling payments; the start-up cost is low; and you have huge flexibility to promote how you want. It’s one of the easiest ways to make money from the web.

As my business grew and technology progressed, I went on to develop other things like software, webinar trainings, and iPhone apps. Now, it seems like many things I touch turn to gold. Meaning, I'm confident I can go into any market and create dollars from scratch. I've been doing this awhile and am able to spot trends very early on.

I hope this post inspired you. 

The wheels should be turning in your mind by now. There's no reason why you can't do this stuff. It's all about working smart, accessing the best tools and having the right mentorship. My door is always open.

Procrastination only pushes profits into the future. With where this economy is headed, you want to bank sooner rather than later. The window of opportunity is getting smaller and that's by design.  

Having just one flow of income is risky. These three methods have been reliable over the years. Use them wisely.

What if the most important measure of college success is not whether students enroll in college, but how quickly they complete it? 

For decades, educators have worked to expand college access for students historically underrepresented in higher education. Far fewer have asked a more ambitious question: What would it take for students to earn a college credential while many of their peers are still finding their footing in college? 

The P-TECH Brooklyn Pathways in Technology Early College High School Class of 2019 offers a compelling answer. While 65% of graduates met CUNY's college-ready benchmark, nearly one-third earned a STEM associate degree within two years of high school graduation, suggesting that the future of educational equity lies not just in opening the door to college, but in accelerating students through it.

SARANG HELICOPTER DISPLAY TEAM TO DAZZLE BAREILLY AFTER EIGHT YEARS

Bareilly | 13-17 October 2026

The Indian Air Force’s renowned Sarang Helicopter Display Team will perform in Bareilly from 13 to 17 October 2026, marking its return to the city after its last performance in 2018. The much-anticipated event will offer students from various schools, colleges and invited members of the civil community an opportunity to witness one of the most distinctive aerial display teams in the world.

Sarang, the helicopter aerobatic display team of the Indian Air Force, holds the unique distinction of being amongst the world’s very few military display teams. Flying the indigenously designed and manufactured Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv, the team showcases extraordinary precision in close-formation flying that demands exceptional skills, discipline and teamwork. The spectacular display reflects not only the proficiency of its pilots but also the growing capabilities of India’s indigenous aerospace industry.

Since its inception, Sarang has represented the Indian Air Force at prestigious national and international air shows, captivating audiences with its breathtaking performances. The vibrant helicopters, symbolic of the peacock from which the team derives its name, embody grace, courage and national pride.

The performance of Sarang is particularly significant as it brings the excellence of military aviation closer to the people. For the youth, especially students, witnessing these remarkable displays can be an inspiring introduction to aviation, science, technology and the possibilities of a career in the Armed Forces. It offers a rare opportunity to see the practical application of teamwork and precision —values that extend well beyond the flying arena.

Through its performances in Bareilly, Sarang will once again seek to inspire young minds, foster a spirit of innovation and adventure, and showcase operational excellence of the Indian Air Force.

text:
Our son was in Miami with some friends Saturday night and left his iPhone in an Uber. It was careless, but I don’t know many people who haven’t misplaced something at some point in their lives.

Yesterday morning, we logged into Find My iPhone and watched that little dot circle the Miami airport over and over again. After about half a dozen trips, we were pretty confident the phone was still in the Uber.

Our son eventually reached the driver, who offered to bring it back for $200, paid electronically in advance. I wasn’t about to send $200 to someone I didn’t know based on a promise, so I contacted Uber.

The driver later offered to return it for free at midnight when he finished working. And to be fair, I appreciated that offer. But it was still morning, and I was concerned that the longer the phone stayed in a car picking up strangers around Miami, the less likely our son was to get it back. I felt like time wasn’t on our side.

The driver was only 13 miles away, so they offered to come to him, wherever it was convenient. That’s when the price dropped to $100 cash.

I’ve been in business long enough to understand that everyone’s time has value. Had he asked for $30 to bring the phone back, I would’ve understood. But asking for $100 just to hand somebody their own phone when they’re willing to come to you? Hard pass.

Thankfully, our son got his phone back, but I keep thinking about how differently this could’ve gone.

Imagine if the driver had simply said, “I’ve got your phone. I’m working right now, but here’s where you can meet me.”

I’d still be telling this story today, except it would be about a kind Uber driver in Miami who helped our son. I probably would’ve found a way to thank him myself, and I suspect plenty of other people would’ve appreciated what he did, too.

Instead, I’m disappointed that someone saw an opportunity to make $100 rather than an opportunity to help another person. I’m not angry with the guy, and I don’t wish anything bad on him. I don’t know his circumstances, and I don’t believe one disappointing interaction tells you everything about a person. I just wish he’d handled it differently.

I’ve always believed in karma. Not necessarily that every good deed earns an immediate reward, but that how we treat people eventually has a way of catching up with us.

Some of the best things that have happened in my life started with doing something for somebody when there was absolutely nothing in it for me. Sometimes those people returned the favor, sometimes somebody else did, and sometimes nothing happened at all. And that’s fine because doing something good shouldn’t come with an expectation of getting paid back.

But I believe the opposite is true, too. When you make a habit of taking advantage of people, eventually that catches up with you as well.

Here’s something I believe more strongly at 55 than I did at 25: the good you put into this world has a way of coming back around. And unfortunately, so does the bad.

Oh…and good morning! ☀️

SUNNY & WARM DAYS THIS WEEK; COLD FRONT LIKELY FRIDAY; MUCH COOLER THIS WEEKEND... Sunshine and warm/hot afternoons are ahead for south Alabama and northwest Florida this week as recovery from Hurricane Isaias continues. Much cooler air is set to arrive this weekend. High temperatures today will be in the upper 80s to low 90s, with no rain expected. High pressure will keep our weather mostly sunny and dry through midweek. The next meaningful change comes late this week as a cold front approaches, bringing a noticeable drop in temperatures by Saturday and Sunday.

DRY THROUGH THURSDAY; WARM/HOT AFTERNOONS; PLEASANT NIGHTS... Dry weather is expected today, tomorrow, and Wednesday, with rain chances remaining very low Thursday and Friday. Afternoon temperatures will generally reach the upper 80s to low 90s through Thursday. These temperatures could approach our high temperature records in parts of the region. Nights will offer some relief, with lows tonight ranging from the mid 50s to the mid 60s closer to the coast.

HOT TEMPS BUT NOT AS HUMID AS HURRICANE RECOVERY CONTINUES... The warmth is particularly important for anyone working on recovery efforts after Hurricane Isaias or still without power. Even with afternoon humidity keeping the heat index close to the actual temperature, prolonged sunshine and strenuous cleanup work can increase the risk of heat-related illness. Please take frequent breaks in the shade and drink plenty of water.

COLD FRONT ON THE WAY FRIDAY NIGHT... A cold front will likely move through late this week, with a much cooler and drier airmass following behind it. The exact timing of the passage still needs to be refined, but the forecast shows a substantial temperature drop between Friday and Saturday. Limited moisture ahead of the front should keep rain coverage minimal. This looks more like a change in temperatures than a significant rain event, with rain chances remaining at 10% or less through the weekend.

MUCH COOLER THIS WEEKEND WITH PLENTY OF SUNSHINE... Much more comfortable afternoons are ahead for Saturday and Sunday! High temperatures will fall into the mid to upper 70s Saturday, followed by low to mid 70s Sunday. Drier air behind the front should allow plenty of sunshine, with most communities remaining rain-free. Sunday morning lows will range from around 50° in the coolest locations to the mid 60s in warmer spots. A welcome change after the very warm afternoons this week.

TROPICS: GULF & CARIBBEAN QUIET... The National Hurricane Center is not highlighting any disturbances in the Gulf or Caribbean Sea that could become named tropical storms in the days ahead. Isaias has been post-tropical since Friday night after landfall, and NHC has issued its final advisory.

TROPICS: DISTURBANCE IN ATLANTIC... The one disturbance being monitored for possible tropical storm formation in the Atlantic basin is in the eastern Atlantic, a few hundred miles southwest of the Cabo Verde Islands. NHC indicates a low, 20% chance of development over the next 7 days. Showers and thunderstorms remain disorganized, and stronger upper-level winds should limit development by midweek. Heavy rain will be possible over portions of the Cabo Verde Islands as the system moves slowly northward to north-northwestward.

An election introduces a variable capable of reshaping those relationships... a renewed political mandate with the authority to renegotiate the agreements, financing and security arrangements surrounding Ukraine...

Now connect the Poland–Ukraine land bridge, American military positioning, emerging energy corridors and hundreds of billions in reconstruction capital...

Every new sovereign option changes the dependency structure... redistributing leverage across the entire network...

Trump and Putin have now placed Ukraine's political mandate into the equation... and the game is already changing before a single vote is cast...

text:
Mohsen Zanganeh, who chairs Iran’s parliamentary economic commission, used a trip to Afghanistan to praise the Taliban authorities and call Pakistan “hypocritical.” He even claimed Witkoff handed Shehbaz Sharif his April 8 post. Look at what that post announced: a ceasefire, agreed barely an hour before Trump’s deadline to destroy Iran’s power plants and bridges, after Trump said he acted on calls from Sharif and Field Marshal Munir. Islamabad then hosted 21 hours of talks across three rounds, and Guterres has since credited Pakistan with the April ceasefire and the June memorandum.

The charge that Pakistan can’t be trusted because it talks to Washington and Riyadh gets it backwards. A mediator with no line to Trump is a bystander, and Tehran accepted Islamabad because it could reach both sides. Pakistan was also consistent, condemning the US-Israeli strikes that opened the war on February 28 and Iran’s attacks on Gulf states.

Nor does the stalled deal point at the mediator. Iran says it won’t give up enrichment, Vance wants meaningful cuts, and Trump rejected Tehran’s latest offer. Those are the principals’ red lines, not Pakistan’s drafting.

The record of the all-or-nothing camp is worse: Assad gone, Hezbollah’s leadership gutted in 2024, Iran’s supreme leader killed in the opening strikes, and over 74,200 dead in Gaza. Zanganeh’s own Herat visit was a trade-and-transit pitch, which is not a strategy.

TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE RUSSIA–UKRAINE “ENERGY CEASEFIRE.” UKRAINE SAYS ATTACKS CONTINUE. WHERE IS THE AGREEMENT?

Updated: October 12, 2026

President Donald Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate ceasefire covering energy infrastructure.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the announcement was news to him.

Ukrainian officials then reported continued Russian strikes on energy facilities.

Russia had not publicly confirmed the agreement as of early Monday.

WHAT WE KNOW

On October 11, Trump declared on Truth Social that both countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire effective immediately.

But no joint agreement, verification mechanism, duration or detailed terms accompanied the announcement.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine would support stopping attacks on Russian energy facilities if Moscow stopped attacking Ukraine’s infrastructure.

He also said Kyiv was awaiting details from Washington.

Ukrainian officials reported further Russian attacks, including against energy infrastructure in Kharkiv.

That establishes a critical distinction:

An announced ceasefire is not the same as a mutually confirmed, implemented ceasefire.

Source — Reuters:
https://t.co/2Ujc9Hbe69

THE SEPARATE RUSSIAN DIESEL DEAL

Days earlier, Trump announced an arrangement with Vladimir Putin to release more than 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel into American and global markets, with additional supplies promised.

The administration says the arrangement could help ease elevated fuel prices.

But six U.S. senators—four Republicans and two Democrats—called for the plan to be reversed.

They argue it conflicts with restrictions Congress established on Russian energy imports following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

The administration maintains it has legal authority to provide sanctions relief.

The legal dispute has not been conclusively resolved.

Energy analysts also question whether the announced supply would materially reduce American fuel prices. The initial volume is small compared with global demand, and delivery timing matters.

Source — AP:
https://t.co/vf24e9Hfl5

KEY PERSPECTIVES

Trump administration: An energy ceasefire could reduce attacks on infrastructure, while additional diesel supplies could ease fuel prices.

Ukraine: A reciprocal ceasefire is welcome, but Russian compliance must be demonstrated. Ukraine says attacks continued after the announcement.

Russia: No public confirmation of the claimed agreement had been identified as of early October 12.

Bipartisan Senate critics: Relaxing restrictions on Russian diesel could provide Moscow additional revenue while its war continues.

Energy analysts: Additional supply may offer limited market relief, but the announced volumes do not establish a substantial or lasting reduction in retail prices.

EVIDENCE STATUS

CONFIRMED: Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire; Zelenskyy publicly awaited details; Ukrainian officials reported continued strikes; the Russian diesel plan drew bipartisan congressional objections.

REPORTED, NOT INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED: The full extent and timing of strikes following the announcement.

UNRESOLVED: Whether both governments agreed to specific terms, whether an enforceable ceasefire exists, the legal status of the diesel arrangement and its actual price effects.

NOT ESTABLISHED: That attacks have stopped, that Russia accepted a verified reciprocal agreement, or that the diesel arrangement will meaningfully lower U.S. fuel prices.

TRUTH MATTERS TAKEAWAY

A genuine halt to energy-infrastructure attacks could protect Ukrainian civilians and reduce damage ahead of winter.

But diplomatic announcements must be distinguished from agreements that both parties acknowledge and actually follow.

And efforts to lower fuel prices must be examined alongside sanctions law, Russian energy revenues and the real scale of promised supply.

The ceasefire has been announced. Its implementation has not been established.

Facts first. Context second. You decide.
