text:
Elon Musk was beaten so badly by bullies at his school in South Africa that he was hospitalized. He was thrown down a flight of concrete stairs and kicked in the head until he lost consciousness. He was 13 years old. The attack was so severe that he had difficulty breathing through his nose for years afterward and eventually required surgery to repair the damage.

The bullying was not a single incident. It was systematic. Daily. For years. He was the smallest kid in his year. He was the one who read encyclopedias instead of playing sports. He was the one who corrected teachers in class. In the social hierarchy of a South African boys' school in the 1980s, these traits did not earn respect. They earned violence.

He has described the experience as the most formative period of his life. Not the companies. Not the billions. Not the rockets. The years of being beaten by children who hated him for being different. He told an interviewer that there were days he was afraid to go to school. The man who would later challenge entire industries and governments was afraid to walk through a school gate.

His father, by multiple accounts, offered no protection. When Elon came home bruised and bleeding, the response was not comfort. It was indifference or, worse, the suggestion that he deserved it. The one place a child expects safety, home, offered the same emotional climate as the schoolyard. Nowhere was safe.

The man who builds rockets that survive re entry through temperatures that would melt steel was once a boy who couldn't survive a school day without being hit. The resilience the world admires didn't come from success. It was forged in a schoolyard in Pretoria by children who had no idea they were shaping the most consequential person of their generation.

The bullies are still in South Africa. The boy they hospitalized employs 130,000 people and is building a city on Mars. The violence made him harder than the people who inflicted it. That was not the outcome they intended.

text:
GOLD OR BITCOIN? I THINK WE’RE ASKING THE WRONG QUESTION.

I've gone back and forth on this debate, and honestly, I understand why people on both sides feel strongly about it.

Bitcoin has a serious argument.

There will only ever be 21 million BTC. No government can simply decide to print more Bitcoin, and no single institution controls the network. For people worried about inflation, currency debasement, and financial systems they don't fully trust, that matters.

But there's one thing Bitcoin doesn't have yet: a long history.

Bitcoin has existed since 2009. That's impressive for a digital asset, but it's still a relatively short period compared with the thousands of years humans have used gold to preserve and transfer wealth.

Gold has passed through wars, changing currencies, political upheavals, and the collapse of monetary systems. It has survived different civilizations and economic arrangements because its value isn't tied to one government, one company, or one financial network.

That doesn't mean gold always goes up. Its price fluctuates, and it can lose purchasing power over certain periods. Bitcoin has also delivered extraordinary returns during its short history, although with significant volatility.

The difference, to me, is that gold has a much longer record of being valued across generations. Bitcoin offers a different kind of scarcity, but its long-term behaviour through major economic and political upheavals is still something we have to wait and see.

So why must owning one mean rejecting the other?

This is where I find $GGBR interesting.

Gold has traditionally been harder to access in small amounts. Buying physical gold can involve dealers, premiums, storage, and the problem of safely keeping it. Bitcoin, on the other hand, can be held in a digital wallet and transferred across the internet.

@goldfishggbr is trying to bring some of that convenience to gold.

Each $GGBR token represents 1/1,000 of a troy ounce of gold-linked value, with its backing structured through I-ON Digital's https://t.co/VLvu4cLSDz gold-backed assets and the Goldfish reserve arrangements. It trades on-chain, allowing people to hold and transfer gold-linked value through crypto infrastructure.

That distinction matters: $GGBR isn't Bitcoin, and holding a token isn't identical to holding a gold bar yourself. Its backing, legal structure, redemption conditions, and smart-contract risks still matter.

But the idea is worth paying attention to.

You can believe in Bitcoin's fixed supply and still want exposure to gold's long history. You can appreciate digital assets without assuming every valuable asset has to be created on a blockchain.

Personally, I don't think the goal should be to win an argument on the internet about which asset is superior.

It's to understand what each asset offers, what risks come with it, and how it might fit into your own approach to preserving wealth.

Gold has history. Bitcoin has digital scarcity. Neither is risk-free, and neither needs to be dismissed for the other to make sense.

Maybe the better question isn't gold or Bitcoin. Maybe it's why we'd limit ourselves to one when they offer two very different things.

That's the part of the $GGBR idea that interests me

text:
JUDGE GOVERNANCE ROBOTICS MICROCHIP — WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT?

Most robotics microchips are designed to compute, perceive, navigate or control motion. The Judge Governance Robotics Microchip is being designed for a different responsibility: deciding whether an AI-powered robot is authorised to perform a specific physical action before that action reaches its actuators.

An AI system might request that a robotic arm lift an object, a warehouse robot enter a restricted zone, or a humanoid approach a person. Judge’s proposed chip would examine the action, the robot’s identity, its permitted capabilities, the current spatial context, sensor freshness and applicable policies. Only a valid decision could produce a cryptographically bound, single-use authorisation for that exact action.

The concept draws on engineering principles from eleven Judge systems, particularly JudgeOS, JudgeSentinel Nexus, Tessera Robotics and Judge Global. The goal is to combine deterministic decisions, non-bypassable execution admission, tamper-evident receipts, replayable evidence and threat awareness in specialised hardware.

Crucially, governance would not replace the robot’s independent safety controller. Safety-rated systems must still manage emergency stops, protective separation, speed limits and motor interlocks. The governance chip would address a complementary question: not merely whether a movement can be performed safely, but whether this AI, under this authority, should be permitted to attempt it at all.

Existing platforms from NVIDIA, Arm and Texas Instruments already offer sophisticated robotics processing, functional-safety features and security hardware. Judge’s proposed differentiation is a dedicated, potentially cross-platform governance-to-actuation authorisation layer.

If demonstrated, it could give robotics developers a reusable foundation for auditable physical AI across different machines. But the custom chip, hardware enforcement, performance and safety integration still require FPGA prototypes, independent testing and validation.

The ambition is straightforward: AI proposes. Governance decides. Independent safety enforces.

text:
Ten million dollars was waiting for me on the other side of the world. 

All I had to do was get on a plane.
I couldn't go.

Not "didn't want to."  Couldn't.

The company I'd started in my den — nights and weekends at first, mailing diskettes from the kitchen table — had grown into a real business with real offices and more than two million customers. A publicly traded California company wanted to buy it, and after months of due diligence, audits, and lawyers, the deal was nearly done. One task remained: fly to Jaipur, India, and personally introduce our American buyer to our overseas software partner, a company run by my good friend Shrishail, who had built some of our most popular products. A handshake trip. A victory lap. The kind of moment founders dream about.

I had never flown overseas, and even a domestic flight takes a toll that I try not to let anyone see. This trip meant days in an unfamiliar country with none of my routines, capped by a midnight bus trek through the countryside on a road the locals cheerfully called the "Road of Death." 

From the moment it was proposed, something deep and inaccessible in me began to panic. And here is the part I couldn't explain to anyone, then or for years afterward: I wasn't afraid of the airplane, and I wasn't afraid of the road. I was afraid of myself. I knew — with the certainty of an engineer reading a gauge — that somewhere between the airport and the negotiating table I would come apart, the kind of collapse my wife and I privately called an "episode," in front of the exact people who were deciding whether to write the check. I honestly didn't think I was well enough to go. I could not have told you what "well" meant, or what, precisely, I had instead.

Understand: I am not a timid man. I had dropped out of high school and clawed my way from a 7-Eleven in Saskatchewan to Microsoft. I routinely risked a million dollars a month on advertising and slept just fine. I'd been sued by the state attorney general and lived to tell the tale. Whatever this was, it wasn't cowardice and it wasn't nerves. It was some kind of hard limit — a ceiling I could feel but couldn't see. And skipping the trip might look strange enough to spook the buyer and sink the whole acquisition: life-changing money if it closed, a devastating loss if it didn't, like misplacing a winning lottery ticket.

That's when a trusted friend saved the day. Allen, a former U.S. Marine who ran our marketing division (I'd recruited him from Microsoft years before) already handled our Indian partners, and he offered to make the trip in my place. It made sense in every way but the one that mattered: I am nearly incapable of delegating anything important, and this was the most important trip of my life. I was now gambling my future, my retirement, and my family's security on another man's performance, all to avoid getting on an airplane. When you catch yourself doing the math on that trade — and taking it anyway — some part of you begins to suspect that what you have is not just a quirk.

Allen made the trip and performed brilliantly. The deal closed a few weeks later. I accelerated the vesting of the employees' stock options so the team — Allen in particular — could share in the sale alongside me, say my goodbyes, and take one last long look around the offices. I handed in my keys and went home with a check that meant I'd never have to work again. By most measures by which a life can be scored, I had just won.

And nobody — least of all me — thought to ask the obvious question: what kind of man stakes his entire fortune on a proxy rather than take a trip? What was that ceiling I'd been living under, and how long had it been there?

It took another decade before I asked, and the answer turned out to have a name. I have autism. I found out long after the career, long after the company, long after the check had cleared. What follows is, in part, the story of how I finally got there — and everything I've learned since about the invisible thing that had been quietly running my life all along.

[This is the new intro to my Second Edition of “Secrets of the Autistic Millionaire”, everything I now know about living a successful life with autism that I wish I had known long ago.] 

Check it out here: https://t.co/J7I8oiQuwW

Love to get your feedback on this new introduction!]

California Expansion Watch — $700 million steel mill moves forward — with more than $47 million in government incentives.

Seems the Golden State is giving up the golden goose to keep business in California. 

Take for example the first new steel mill in more than 50 years, reling heavily on taxpayers financing and incentives. 

The Pacific Steel Group confirmed today that its massive Mojave Micro Mill in Kern County remains on schedule, although the projected construction cost has climbed from $540 million to approximately $700 million.

It's expected to support approximately 700 jobs, with commercial operations scheduled for late August 2027.

Here's the taxpayer angle.

California previously awarded the company a $30 million corporate tax credit, plus a $14 million state energy-storage grant supporting the project.

Now Kern County supervisors have approved an additional incentive worth up to $3.375 million, tied to creating 450 local jobs.

That's more than $47 million in combined government support. You can't buy stock and share in the project's success, Pacific Steel is a private company.

The company says the mill will strengthen California's steel supply chain and create well-paying manufacturing jobs.

But we can reasonably ask why Sacramento offers multimillion-dollar tax breaks to selected corporations while ordinary California taxpayers and smaller businesses receive no comparable project-specific incentives.

text:
Are you ready to Grow Zambia?

Global investors are rapidly positioning themselves to capture the upside of the Grow Zambia Agenda, yet many local citizens risk being sidelined in their own economy. The agenda’s ambitious “10-10-5-3-3-1-1-1” targets that we all know by now, are expected to add roughly $65 billion to the annual economic output. Foreign capital is moving aggressively to back these targets, while local participation is often hampered by capital deficits and technological gaps.  

​To move from spectators to active participants, Zambian entrepreneurs and businesses must leverage joint ventures (JVs) to bridge the local capital deficit and import advanced technology.

​Here is how you can position yourself to be bankable, investment-ready, and the ideal local partner for global capital:

​1. Formalise Your Corporate Governance

​Global capital cannot flow into informal structures. To be bankable, your business must operate with transparent financial records, be tax compliant, and have clear ownership structures. Transitioning from a "hustle" to a structured corporate entity with audited financials reduces the perceived risk for foreign partners and institutional lenders.

​2. Bring Tangible Local Value to the Table

​In a joint venture, the foreign partner typically brings affordable capital, specialised expertise, and scaling technology. As the Zambian partner, you must offer strategic value beyond simply holding a passport. Your leverage comes from...

- ​Operational Assets: Secured land titles, existing licenses, or operational facilities.

- ​Market Access: Deep understanding of the local supply chain, established distribution networks, and off-take agreements.

- ​Regulatory Navigation: Proven capability to manage local compliance, community relations, and sector-specific regulations.

​3. Align Directly with the Grow Zambia Targets

​Capital flows toward national priorities. Position your business to solve the supply chain bottlenecks of the Grow Zambia Agenda. If the goal is 10 million tonnes of maize and 3 million tonnes of soya beans, look at agro-processing, cold-chain logistics, and fertilizer distribution. If the target is 5 million tourist arrivals, focus on hospitality infrastructure and tech enabled booking services. Investors want to fund businesses that ride the momentum of these macro-economic goals.

​4. Structure for Mutual Protection

​A successful joint venture requires robust legal frameworks. Ensure your partnership agreements clearly define equity splits, dispute resolution mechanisms, and technology transfer clauses. The goal is not just to secure funding, but to ensure that operational knowledge and technological capability are permanently transferred to your local team.  

​Zambia's wealth creation over the next five years will be driven by those who can combine local insight with global resources. By prioritising bankability and strategic partnerships, Zambian citizens can secure their stake in the nation's economic expansion.

Let's be bold. Let’s Grow Zambia together!

text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
I think there's a serious bubble forming around Ukraine style defense tech. We're increasingly shaping US defense priorities around Ukraine's battlefield requirements rather than our own.

Ukraine is projected to produce 6-7 MILLION FPVs this year. The Pentagon's Drone Dominance program is targeting just over 200,000 purchases by 2027.

For some reason American companies are racing to build factories capable of producing at Ukrainian wartime scale. Maybe its because the OSC has even offered up to $820M in conditional financing to expand domestic drone component production.

Can someone please help me understand who's actually going to buy all this capacity, given we won't even have the price advantage?

Ukraine consumes millions of FPVs because it's fighting a continuous land war against a neighboring country. Its UGVs perform tens of thousands of frontline resupply and evacuation missions for the same reason.

The US shares land borders with Canada and Mexico. Neither is (yet) a conventional military adversary.

Our biggest challenges are overseas. A war with China or the middle east, involves thousands of miles of ocean, contested logistics, proxy wars, naval warfare, missile defense, hopefully low cost ballistic missiles, and protecting forward deployed forces. A fiber optic FPV with a 10-20km spool does not solve those challenges nearly as much as it helps Ukraine's problem set.

Short range FPVs have applications once forces or infrastructure are forward deployed. UGVs do too. But Ukraine needing millions of them annually doesn't mean the US does at all.

An area I believe the Pentagon is moving correctly on defense: JIATF 401 is accelerating cUAS procurement to protect American facilities and forces. That's a very perpendicular mission from producing millions of one way drones to attack targets along a static frontline.

My concern is that we're heading toward what I like to call "the Great FPV Consolidation," potentially mirroring the wave of M&A activity we saw in the 90s. Companies are scaling production around Ukrainian wartime consumption rates, but it's unclear to me whether sustained American demand will be enough to support them all.

There's an argument for building surge capacity ahead of demand, particularly given our dependence on foreign components. But surge capacity and a sustainable business model aren't necessarily the same thing.

@PalmerLuckey @JTLonsdale @jamoses92 @davidu - Would really value your perspectives on the unit economics and long term demand here given your experiences building and investing in defense. Am I underestimating the long term market, or do you see significant consolidation and company failures as the Ukraine driven defense tech sector matures?

text:
The first reading for Monday October 12, 2026: Book of Galatians (Galatians 4:22-24, 26-27, 31–5:1)

Abraham had two sons. One from the slave woman and one from the free woman

These women represent two covenants one of slavery from Sinai and one of freedom

Believers are children of the free woman and must stand firm without submitting to slavery again

This is the message of Galatians 4:22-24, 26-27, 31-5:1

Discovering the Freedom Christ Offers to Faithful Believers

The letter to the Galatians stands as a powerful reminder that Christ came to liberate believers from the burdens of the law and to invite them into a life of grace filled with genuine relationship with God. This message resonates deeply with practicing Catholics who seek to live out their faith amid the distractions and demands of daily life. Through careful reflection on the text we see how the apostle Paul urges the community to stand firm in the liberty purchased by the cross rather than slipping back into old patterns of self justification. Such freedom calls each person to trust in divine mercy while embracing the responsibilities that flow from it. In this way the reading encourages a balanced approach that honors both the gift of salvation and the call to holiness.

What Does It Mean to Be Set Free from the Law

Paul addresses the Galatians with urgency because some among them were turning back to the requirements of the Mosaic law as a means of earning favor with God. He reminds them that the law served its purpose in the past yet now finds its fulfillment in Christ who has opened a new path. This shift means that believers no longer measure their worth by strict adherence to external rules alone but instead rest in the promise of faith. Catholics today can relate to this tension when they feel pulled between ritual observance and personal devotion. The text invites a deeper trust that the sacraments and traditions of the Church flow from this freedom rather than contradict it. By understanding this context the faithful can avoid the trap of legalism that stifles joy and growth in the spiritual life.

How Does Faith Shape Our Daily Walk with God

The reading emphasizes that justification comes through faith in Jesus Christ and not through works of the law. This teaching does not dismiss good deeds but places them in proper perspective as the fruit of belief rather than the root. For Catholics this aligns with the understanding that grace initiates the relationship and prompts works of charity and justice. Paul uses the example of Abraham to show that faith has always been the foundation of right standing before God. In practical terms this means approaching prayer the Eucharist and acts of service with a heart open to divine initiative. Such an outlook prevents the discouragement that arises when one relies solely on personal effort. The result is a steadier journey marked by gratitude and perseverance.

Why Must We Resist Returning to Old Bondages

Paul warns against using freedom as an opportunity for the flesh which could lead to division and self indulgence within the community. Instead he calls believers to serve one another through love as the fulfillment of the law. This balance protects the gift of liberty from misuse and directs it toward building up the body of Christ. In contemporary Catholic life this caution applies to avoiding extremes of either rigid rule following or casual disregard for moral teachings. The text encourages ongoing conversion that keeps the heart centered on Christ. When temptations arise to revert to old ways of thinking the faithful can recall the cross as the source of true release. This resistance strengthens communal bonds and fosters authentic witness to the gospel.

How Can We Cultivate the Fruits of the Spirit in Everyday Life

The reading contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruits of the Spirit which include love joy peace patience kindness generosity faithfulness gentleness and self control. These qualities emerge naturally when one lives by faith rather than by compulsion. Catholics find support for this growth in the sacraments and in regular examination of conscience. Paul makes clear that such fruits are not achieved through human striving alone but through cooperation with the grace already received. This perspective offers encouragement during seasons of struggle or dryness in prayer. By focusing on these virtues the believer experiences a gradual transformation that affects family relationships work and community involvement. The process reminds each person that freedom in Christ is dynamic and ongoing.

The message of Galatians ultimately points toward a life where faith works through love and where the believer stands secure in the liberty won by the Savior. This understanding deepens appreciation for the Churchs teachings and inspires renewed commitment to prayer and service. As the faithful reflect on these words they discover renewed strength to live as children of the promise rather than slaves to fear or performance. The reading continues to guide Catholics toward greater trust in divine mercy and toward the joy that comes from walking in the Spirit.
Living Out the Freedom of Christ in All Your Relationships

In the reading from Galatians the apostle Paul presents a powerful allegory that calls the faithful to embrace spiritual liberty through the contrast between bondage and promise. This passage draws from the story of Abraham's sons to illustrate how believers can move beyond fleshly constraints toward the freedom offered in Christ. Faithful Catholics find in these verses practical guidance for navigating relationships with family members friends neighbors and co-workers in ways that reflect the promise rather than slavery. By reflecting on the themes of freedom and promise individuals discover renewed strength to foster genuine connections grounded in faith. The message encourages standing firm against any form of spiritual slavery that might hinder authentic daily interactions.

How Can the Allegory of Two Covenants Shape Family Conversations

The section from Galatians 4:22-24 explains that Abraham had two sons one by a slave woman and the other by a free woman with one born according to the flesh and the other through the promise. Now this is an allegory these women are two covenants. Faithful Catholics can apply this breakdown in family settings by encouraging discussions that prioritize promise over mere obligation such as guiding children away from competitive rivalries toward mutual support rooted in shared faith. Parents might reference the birth through promise to inspire siblings to resolve conflicts with patience rather than dominance fostering an environment where family members feel liberated to express love without fear of judgment. This approach helps transform everyday meals or gatherings into moments where the contrast between slavery and freedom becomes a living lesson that strengthens household bonds over time.

What Benefits Arise When Friends Embrace the Freedom of the Jerusalem Above

Galatians 4:26-27 shifts focus to the Jerusalem above which is free and corresponds to the mother of believers quoting rejoice you childless one you who bear no children burst into song and shout you who endure no birth pangs for the children of the desolate woman are more numerous than the children of the one who is married. In friendships this analysis encourages Catholics to celebrate the expansive nature of spiritual freedom by supporting friends through challenges with words that lift burdens rather than impose expectations. One might share this imagery during casual talks to remind a friend struggling with past regrets that true liberty comes from Christ allowing relationships to grow in joy and resilience instead of repeating cycles of dependency. Such interactions build communities of encouragement where friends stand together as children of the promise leading to deeper trust and mutual inspiration in daily life.

How Does Standing Firm Against Slavery Transform Neighborly Exchanges

The passage continues in Galatians 4:31 with so then friends we are children not of the slave but of the free woman setting the stage for active resistance to any yoke of bondage in broader community ties. Catholics interacting with neighbors can break down this idea by choosing responses that promote freedom such as offering help without strings attached or listening without judgment during fence-line conversations or community events. This section of the reading inspires acts like mediating local disputes with fairness drawn from the promise rather than fleshly disputes ensuring that neighborhood relations reflect the liberty Christ provides. Over repeated encounters this mindset turns potential conflicts into opportunities for witness where neighbors experience the expansive family of faith through consistent compassionate presence.

For freedom Christ set us free so stand firm and do not submit again to the yoke of slavery.

In What Ways Can Co-Workers Experience the Promise Through Professional Conduct

Finally Galatians 5:1 reinforces the call to stand firm in freedom which Catholics can extend to workplace dynamics by modeling integrity that rejects manipulative pressures or unethical shortcuts. Analyzing the full arc from allegory to exhortation helps professionals apply the promise in meetings or collaborations by prioritizing fairness and encouragement that liberates colleagues from competitive slavery. This leads to environments where co-workers feel valued as part of a larger promise rather than trapped in cycles of performance anxiety fostering productivity rooted in mutual respect. Such applications ensure that faith influences career interactions in subtle yet profound ways that witness to enduring liberty.

Spotlighting Key Verses for Daily Inspiration in Varied Interactions

Specific quotes from the passage offer direct tools for these relationships with the allegory in verses 22 through 24 reminding all groups to choose promise over flesh in conversations. The imagery of the free woman in verses 26 and 27 can be gently introduced in family or friend talks to highlight growth through faith while the declaration in 4:31 and 5:1 serves as a quiet anchor during neighbor or co-worker moments of tension. These elements together equip believers to live the reading fully across contexts.

Through consistent reflection on this passage faithful Catholics cultivate lives marked by the freedom Christ intends allowing relationships to flourish in promise rather than constraint.

Thank you for praying today with RCatholicPrayer your fellow pilgrim on the path of repentance and conversion.

A fellow penitent seeking God's grace,

text:
🎨 LOUIS FRATINO
Coffee, 2026 🫘☕️🗣️ 
Oil on canvas • 152.7 × 182.9 cm 🖌️
Exhibited in Prose, David Zwirner, London

A Crowded Counter, a Child’s Reach & the Life Around a Cup

▸ ▸ ▸

The coffee is the smallest thing happening here.

Louis Fratino fills this café with bodies leaning, hands occupied, faces turned toward different interests. A server balances a plate. Customers lift cups. A child reaches into a world arranged at adult height. Below them, two dogs conduct their own introductions.

The room is crowded, but our attention keeps finding somewhere particular to settle.

Coffee catches a familiar pleasure: being among people whose lives briefly overlap with ours, without needing to know the whole story of anyone at the counter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🎨 COLOUR AND LIGHT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The pale blue counter gives the painting its broadest stretch of cool colour. It curves through the warm room, carrying our eye past cups, saucers, plates, and hands.

Behind it, reds and reddish browns gather around the shelves and bottles. The contrast makes the counter feel almost luminous. Fratino distributes brightness through objects and clothing rather than relying on a single dramatic beam of light.

The child’s yellow clothes provide the clearest interruption. That concentrated warmth pulls us toward the centre, while blue, green, and pink clothing lead us outward again.

Small white cups repeat across the scene. Their rims and handles create a scattered rhythm of circles among the longer curves of shoulders, arms, and backs. An ordinary piece of crockery becomes part of the room’s visual timing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🌀 THE COUNTER HOLDS THE CROWD TOGETHER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The horseshoe-shaped counter is the painting’s organizing gesture. Follow its edge and the apparent jumble becomes surprisingly legible.

It separates the people serving from the people being served, while bringing both groups into a continuous exchange. A plate crosses the gap. A hand reaches over it. Someone leans closer.

The viewpoint is deliberately unsettled. We look down across the tabletop and into the floor space, while nearby faces press forward with an intimacy that a more distant view would lose.

The room seems tilted toward us. Its people overlap without settling neatly into a single, orderly depth.

That compression gives the café its physical character. We experience the small negotiations of a busy interior: where to put an elbow, how to turn, how much room another person needs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🤲 THE CHILD CHANGES THE SCALE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The child in yellow gives the whole room a different measurement.

For the adults, the counter is somewhere to lean, drink, work, or wait. For the child, it is a height to overcome. Raised arms make that difference visible without requiring a story to explain it.

The bright clothing catches us first. The reach keeps us looking.

We do not need to decide exactly what the child wants. The effort itself is enough: a small person stretching toward the level at which everyone else appears to conduct their business.

That detail keeps the crowd from becoming merely a pattern of attractive shapes. Fratino gives us a body with a particular relationship to the room.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🐕 COMPANY WITHOUT A SINGLE STORY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The dogs near the bottom of the painting offer another change of scale. Beneath the cups and conversations, they face one another in the narrow space between human legs.

At floor level, the social arrangements seem to be proceeding perfectly well.

Above them, the people remain absorbed in different things. Some turn inward toward the counter. Others present their backs or profiles. The figure in pink at the right brings a hand toward the mouth; nearby, a bespectacled drinker holds a small cup.

These gestures do not resolve into one central incident. Their coexistence is the subject.

To me, the warmth comes from that freedom. The painting allows people to share a place without requiring them to share a mood. Closeness includes distraction, appetite, work, and the pleasure of being left alone among others.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🖌️ A ROOM BUILT FROM MARKS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The floor is especially lively. Ochre, cream, and brown strokes divide it into uneven lengths and angles. Its pattern pushes upward through the open space, keeping even the gaps between bodies active.

Clothing adds other rhythms. Stripes, checks, dark jackets, and pale sleeves give adjacent figures different visual textures. Strong contours hold the bodies together while allowing their proportions to stretch and bend.

The gallery connects the exhibition’s communal scenes with Leon Kossoff’s urban paintings. That reference is useful here: the density of a shared place becomes something the painter builds into the handling of bodies and space.

Fratino offers another way into his work:

❝ Painting feels like this place to talk about things I don’t have the words for. ❞
— Louis Fratino, Louisiana Channel, 2026

Coffee gives that thought a setting. We recognize the feeling of this room through the spacing of its people, the tilt of a head, and the little area someone has made for a cup. Nobody needs to deliver a speech about belonging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⚖️ MY CRITICAL JUDGMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The painting’s strongest achievement is its movement between the crowd and the individual gesture. The counter gathers everyone into a shared composition; the child’s reach and the drinkers’ occupied hands keep returning us to particular lives.

Its compression also creates resistance. Bodies can feel wedged together, and the tilted space initially reads more easily as a dense pattern than as a room we could enter. That can delay our sense of each person’s separate presence.

Yet the distortions remain connected to something recognizable. A busy café rarely gives us a clean, uninterrupted view. We encounter it through partial faces, passing hands, nearby backs, and whatever we can see around somebody’s shoulder.

Fratino makes that abundance worth staying with. The longer we look, the more the crowd becomes company.

▸ ▸ ▸

👁️ A useful way to look: Follow the pale counter from the foreground around its curve. Then return to the child in yellow and let your eye drop to the dogs. Notice how the same room becomes a different place at each height.

The cup is small. The life around it keeps expanding.

text:
Washington State 

WORKERS COMP INSURANCE 

WA State Dept. of Labor and Industries (L&I)

Washington State Proposes 4.9% Workers’ Compensation Rate Hike for 2027

Oct. 12, 2026

Premium Increase to Address Rising Medical and Wage Replacement Costs Reserve Funds Bridge Gap to Limit Full Cost Pass-Through

The Washington State Department of Labor & Industries, known widely as L&I, has formally unveiled a proposed 4.9% rise in workers’ compensation premium rates scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. This adjustment follows a thorough review of the system’s financial outlook, claims experience, and broader economic indicators, and is designed to ensure the state’s vital workplace safety and injury support programme remains fully funded and sustainable for years to come. Should the proposal be adopted following the public input period, the average cost of coverage will increase by approximately $1.44 per week for each full-time employee across the state, with employers contributing roughly 75% of that additional amount and workers covering the remaining 25% through their respective shares of the premium. While the percentage change appears measured, it touches every industry and workforce in Washington, making it a matter of genuine consequence for business owners, employees, and families alike.

The driving forces behind the increase are deep-seated and persistent. Medical costs continue to rise across the United States and within Washington specifically, reflecting higher prices for prescription drugs, advanced diagnostic procedures, surgical interventions, rehabilitation services, and long-term care, all of which are frequently required when a worker is injured or falls ill due to their job. Beyond healthcare expenses, wage replacement benefits are closely tied to earnings levels, and as average wages throughout the state climb, the value of weekly compensation payments and long-term disability benefits rises in tandem. L&I has made clear that the proposed 4.9% rate increase does not represent the full magnitude of these growing costs. Instead, the agency intends to use funds from the workers’ compensation contingency reserve to cover the substantial difference between what the new rates will generate and what will actually be needed to meet projected claims. This is a deliberate and considered approach: it limits the immediate burden on businesses and workers, spreading the financial impact more gradually and avoiding sudden, disruptive spikes in premium costs, while ensuring that the system’s commitments to injured employees remain fully honoured without interruption.

The contingency reserve itself serves as a critical financial buffer, built up over time precisely to manage periods when incoming revenue falls short of projected outgoings or when costs rise faster than anticipated. Drawing upon it now reflects careful stewardship; the agency is choosing to smooth the transition rather than pass the full cost through at once, but it also underscores that the pressures driving this review are not one-off events. Medical inflation, demographic shifts in the workforce, and the evolving nature of workplace injuries and occupational illnesses are long-term realities that will continue to shape future rate reviews, making this adjustment both a response to current needs and a prudent step toward securing the programme’s financial foundation.

Members of the public, employers, labour organisations, and individual workers now have multiple opportunities to share their perspectives, raise concerns, and offer insights before the final decision is made. 

Two virtual public hearings have been scheduled to allow direct oral testimony: the first beginning at 10 a.m. on October 28, and the second at 2 p.m. on October 29.

text:
🌊 POTOMAC RIVER: DC Water says the Potomac River has returned to normal following a massive sewage spill that dumped more than 240 MILLION GALLONS of wastewater into the river earlier this year.

The environmental emergency began January 19, when a section of the Potomac Interceptor sewer line collapsed along Clara Barton Parkway in Montgomery County.

The rupture contaminated the river, triggered public health warnings, and sent crews scrambling to contain the spill.

NEW TEST RESULTS:

▪️ More than six months of water-quality monitoring found E. coli levels had returned to their normal range.

▪️ Expanded testing began in August at six Maryland locations upstream and downstream of the spill.

▪️ Samples were collected five times and examined for bacteria, oxygen levels, nutrients, and metals.

▪️ All measured indicators were within normal ranges for the river.

▪️ Health advisories and river-access restrictions were lifted as conditions improved.

Emergency repairs were completed in March, but broader rehabilitation of the aging sewer infrastructure continues.

DC Water says the latest results show no current evidence of lasting environmental damage from the spill.

The utility’s leadership also changed following the crisis, with its board voting in June to remove then-CEO David Gadis.

The findings offer encouraging news for boaters, anglers, waterfront businesses, and communities along the Potomac, although the infrastructure failure raises continuing questions about maintenance and oversight.

SOURCES: DC Water

text:
Oct 12, 1870: Robert E. Lee died in Lexington, Virginia, five and a half years after he surrendered at Appomattox.

When the war ended, Lee was the most famous man in the South and he had nothing. His family home at Arlington had been seized by the federal government and turned into a cemetery for Union dead. He was 58, his health was failing, and he was under indictment for treason, though he was never tried.

Offers came in. Businesses wanted to put his name on their letterhead for big salaries. He turned them down. Instead he took a job as president of Washington College, a tiny school in the Shenandoah Valley that had been looted by Union troops during the war. It had a few dozen students and a handful of professors. The salary was $1,500 a year.

He threw himself into it. He knew most of the students by name. He added courses in engineering, business, and journalism, which were unusual for the time. He replaced a long list of rules with an honor system and told students the school had only one rule: every student must be a gentleman.

He spent those years telling Southerners to accept the result of the war. He told former soldiers to go home and rebuild. According to an often-told story, when a widow complained bitterly to him about the Union, he told her not to raise her sons to hate the United States and to make them Americans. In 1869 he paid a short visit to President Ulysses S. Grant at the White House.

His heart was giving out. In the spring of 1870 he took a long trip south, partly for his health. Crowds met him at every stop. On Cumberland Island in Georgia he visited the grave of his father, Revolutionary War hero Light-Horse Harry Lee.

On Sept 28, a cold, rainy day, he went to a long meeting at his church about raising money for the minister's salary. When they came up short, Lee pledged the difference himself. He walked home in the rain and sat down to dinner with his family. When he tried to say grace, no words came out.

He had suffered a stroke. They made a bed for him in the dining room. For two weeks he lay there, mostly silent, while one of the worst floods in Virginia history swept through the region outside.

He died around 9:30 in the morning on Oct 12. He was 63.

Accounts written later said his last words were "Strike the tent," along with an order for A.P. Hill to come up, as if he were back on the battlefield. Doctors who have studied the case think the stroke had taken his ability to speak, and many historians doubt those words were ever said.

The flood had washed away the town undertaker's stock of coffins. Some were found downriver, and the only usable one was too short. Lee was buried in his suit without shoes.

He was laid to rest in a crypt beneath the chapel on the college grounds. Within days the school's trustees voted to rename it Washington and Lee. His horse Traveller, who walked behind the funeral procession, is buried just outside.

After the war Lee had signed an oath of allegiance and applied for a pardon. The oath was lost and never acted on. It was found in the National Archives a century later, and in 1975 Congress restored his citizenship.

Americans still argue over how to remember him and the cause he fought for, and they probably always will. But in the last five years of his life, he chose to spend what he had left teaching young men, rebuilding a broken school, and telling a defeated people to put down their anger and become Americans again.

156 years ago today. Rest easy General.

text:
There seems to be an increasingly casual expectation that countries should immediately capitulate because a greater power demands it. 🌍⚖️

Ukraine should accept Russia’s terms. Canada should accept whatever Washington offers. Greenland should accommodate the ambitions of a larger country.

But having the power to impose a demand does not make that demand legitimate.

The international order built after two devastating world wars rests on a different principle: nations have rights regardless of their size. Sovereignty matters. Borders matter. Agreements matter. Disputes should be resolved through diplomacy and law.

That framework was built in the shadow of enormous sacrifice by veterans and civilians. We honour that sacrifice by defending the principles intended to prevent another generation from enduring the same devastation. 🕊️

🇺🇦 Ukraine can negotiate peace without accepting that an invading power has the right to dictate its territory, leadership or future. A settlement needs Ukrainian participation and credible security, not simply pressure on Ukraine to concede.

🇨🇦 Canada can negotiate constructively with the United States while defending its interests and invoking agreements already in force. CUSMA still exists. Asking that commitments be respected is a legitimate part of negotiation.

🇬🇱 Greenland’s future belongs to its people, within its relationship with Denmark. Strategic importance does not give another country ownership rights. European leaders have explicitly reaffirmed that Denmark and Greenland must decide their future.

These situations differ enormously in severity and legal context. A tariff dispute is not an invasion. But the recurring argument deserves scrutiny: “They’re stronger, so you should give in.”

Of course power matters. Responsible leaders must weigh economic costs, military realities and opportunities for compromise. No country can build policy on wishful thinking.

But negotiation requires agency. Compromise requires consent. A durable agreement requires confidence that its terms will be honoured. 🤝

If the strongest country can discard the rules whenever they become inconvenient, every smaller country becomes less secure. Allies become less trusting. Businesses become less confident. And coercion becomes more attractive because it keeps being rewarded.

The United States helped build this international framework. Defending it is also defending a major American achievement.

We should want diplomacy to succeed, trade to prosper and wars to end. We should also expect powerful countries to respect the rights they demand for themselves.

Our veterans’ sacrifice deserves more than a world where might alone determines what is right. 🌺

#RuleOfLaw #Sovereignty #Diplomacy #Canada #Ukraine

*Rafael Unveils Advanced Defense and Strike Systems at AUSA 2026, Targeting U.S. Military Integration*

Israeli defense giant Rafael Advanced Defense Systems has unveiled a suite of combat-proven and next-generation technologies at the AUSA 2026 exhibition in Washington, D.C., tailored directly to evolving U.S. military procurement needs and operational doctrine.

Among the key disclosures is the SPIKE MCLU2 system, which allows U.S. forces to fire precise SPIKE LR2 missiles directly from existing TOW launchers—long deployed on Bradley fighting vehicles and other platforms—without replacing the gunner interface. The system aims to significantly enhance firepower and troop survivability by extending engagement ranges beyond line-of-sight.

Rafael is also showcasing several next-generation capabilities, including:

• *Sky Sonic:* A full-scale model of its interceptor designed to counter hypersonic missile threats, displayed alongside the Iron Dome's Tamir and David’s Sling's Stunner interceptors.

• *Iron Wasp:* A miniaturized anti-drone interceptor designed to give armored vehicles independent defense against FPV drones and unmanned aerial threats.

• *Samson RWS All-in-One:* A remote weapon station combining a 30mm cannon, dual SPIKE LR2 launchers, and the combat-proven Trophy ("Meil Ru'ach") active protection system.

• *Intelligence & Sensors:* Advanced battlefield situational awareness tools, including the lightweight MicroLite electro-optical/infrared reconnaissance system and Sigma, an RF-based intelligence collection system.

Rafael CEO Yoav Turgeman emphasized the company's readiness to support prolonged high-intensity conflict, stating that the firm offers not only battle-proven operational capabilities but also the scaled production capacity required by the U.S. defense market.

text:
zkCBDC: Microsoft's Chinese Researchers and the Future of Digital Money: The Zero-Knowledge CBDC Patent

A U.S. technology giant, a predominantly China-based research team, and a new architecture for sovereign digital currency reveal how the global struggle over financial privacy is evolving.

On August 25, 2026, the United States Patent and Trademark Office granted Microsoft Technology Licensing U.S. Patent No. 12,719,687, titled Verifiable, Decentralized Zero-Knowledge Central Bank Digital Currency.

The patent describes a potentially significant advancement in digital banking: a system allowing commercial banks to prove that transactions are valid without revealing the underlying financial information. It combines blockchain infrastructure, smart contracts, and zero-knowledge cryptography to create a framework for privacy-preserving central bank digital currencies.

But the most intriguing detail may not be the technology itself.

Nine of the patent's eleven inventors are based in China.

The lead inventor, Srinath Setty, works at Microsoft Research in Redmond, Washington. The remaining team includes researchers in Beijing and Suzhou, reflecting Microsoft's substantial Chinese research presence.

The patent is owned by a U.S. company, but much of the intellectual contribution comes from researchers working in the country that has pursued one of the world's most ambitious sovereign digital-currency programs.

That distinction deserves attention.

China has spent years developing the digital yuan, or e-CNY, while restricting decentralized cryptocurrency trading and mining. Its monetary authorities have sought to combine the efficiency of digital payments with the institutional oversight of a centrally administered currency.

Microsoft's patent addresses precisely the kind of technical problem that becomes important in such a system: how to verify monetary transactions without requiring every participant to expose sensitive financial information.

Then, on September 28, 2026, China's Ministry of State Security reportedly issued a warning that cryptocurrency anonymity is largely an illusion.

The timing creates a remarkable juxtaposition.

China-based researchers working for an American technology company helped invent a privacy-preserving CBDC architecture. Weeks after the patent was granted, China's security establishment publicly emphasized the traceability of conventional cryptocurrencies.

There is no established evidence that the two developments were coordinated. But together, they reveal something important about the future of money.

The emerging competition is not simply between digital currencies and traditional banking. It is between different systems for controlling financial information, monetary issuance, and the authority to transact.

The Microsoft-China Connection Is Central to the Story

Microsoft Research Asia has long been an important center for advanced computer-science research, including cryptography, artificial intelligence, and distributed systems.

The company's Chinese research presence makes the geographic composition of the patent team understandable. Nevertheless, this particular invention occupies an unusually consequential intersection of technology and monetary policy.

China is not merely experimenting with digital payments. It has developed the e-CNY as a sovereign monetary instrument operating within its existing financial system.

Unlike Bitcoin, which eliminates the need for a central issuer, the digital yuan preserves the central bank's authority over monetary issuance.

Unlike Zcash, which allows users to shield transactions on a permissionless blockchain, China's digital-currency framework is designed around regulated participation and controlled anonymity.

The Microsoft patent offers a possible technical solution to one of the challenges confronting such systems.

text:
ZELENSKYY EXPOSES THE PROBLEM WITH TRUMP’S PRESSURE ON UKRAINE 🇺🇦🇺🇸🇷🇺🇭🇺

Why is Ukraine being blamed for a war that Russia started and continues to wage?

Asked about criticism from Donald Trump and Elon Musk, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered an explanation that goes straight to the imbalance at the heart of the current diplomatic pressure.

“Because these people can’t find a key to how to stop Putin. Because it’s more difficult to stop Putin than to pressure others…”

It is easier to demand concessions from a country that depends on your military assistance than to confront an adversary determined to continue fighting. Ukraine needs its partners, and that dependence gives Washington considerable leverage over Kyiv. Putin, meanwhile, has shown little willingness to end the invasion on terms acceptable to Ukraine.

Zelenskyy also challenged attempts to hold Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries responsible for rising energy prices, pointing instead to the war in the Middle East and disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

“It’s simpler to talk about prices and connect them to Ukraine, when everyone in the world understands that prices are rising because of the war in the Middle East and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz.”

Both conflicts can affect energy markets, but the scale of disruption in the Gulf cannot simply be ignored when explaining higher prices to the public.

Zelenskyy ended with a demand for political honesty:

“If we want to speak with people fairly, if we want to be clear, if we want to speak with our nations openly, people have to hear the reality. Don’t play games with people.”

There is a larger issue here than disagreements over fuel prices or diplomatic language.

Ukraine has spent years defending itself against a much larger military power while navigating the political demands of governments whose support it cannot afford to lose. Its leaders must simultaneously fight a war, protect their population and negotiate with partners who sometimes appear more willing to pressure Kyiv than Moscow.

But reducing Ukraine’s ability to resist does not, by itself, remove Russia’s ability or willingness to wage war.

A sustainable peace requires addressing both the military and economic resources that allow the invasion to continue. Otherwise, diplomatic pressure risks becoming a mechanism for extracting concessions from the more vulnerable party.

Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has also faced political controversy over his approach to Ukraine, illustrating how the war has become entangled with domestic political arguments far beyond the battlefield.

Ultimately, Zelenskyy’s argument is not that Ukraine should be exempt from difficult negotiations. It is that the country defending itself should not be treated as the principal obstacle to ending an invasion launched by someone else.

If the objective is genuinely to stop the war, the central question remains how to persuade or compel Russia to stop fighting, rather than how much additional pressure Ukraine can endure.

Recent ecosystem developments have been rapid and multifaceted—ranging from the launch of institutional products and cross-chain asset integration to developer tool upgrades and ongoing regulatory dialogues—collectively signaling a shift toward greater maturity and practical utility.

Canary Funds has launched the first U.S. spot TRX staking ETF (ticker: TRXS). While tracking the spot price of the native token, the fund participates in network validation via Delegated Proof-of-Stake (DPoS) to generate additional yield, with rewards reflected in the net asset value (NAV). This offers investors in traditional markets a compliant pathway to gain both price exposure and on-chain yield, while also underscoring growing recognition of the network's consensus and settlement capabilities.

Ethena’s USDe and sUSDe have been integrated via Stargate, enabling users to directly bridge, hold, and transfer these assets, with plans to expand into further DeFi use cases. Building upon the existing high volume of stablecoin circulation, the addition of synthetic dollar and yield-bearing options enhances the diversity of choices for daily settlement and asset allocation.

Additionally, the story behind the "Justin Sun Prize" was shared: the future belongs to ideas that truly drive the world forward. Supporting innovators lays the groundwork for broader application scenarios and long-term value creation.

Following the integration of Ducat, Bitcoin-native credit can now enter the ecosystem; users can transfer UNIT as wUNIT and exchange it for USDT, while the underlying BTC remains secured on the Bitcoin blockchain. This design decouples credit flow from the security of the original chain, further bridging value channels across different asset systems.

Participating as a Gold Sponsor at the CoinDesk Policy & Regulation Forum in Washington, the network has actively engaged in discussions regarding transparency, on-chain analytics, and public-private collaboration, demonstrating a proactive commitment to aligning with the regulatory landscape and advancing compliance infrastructure.

Privy has expanded its support for wallet and payment infrastructure, providing developers with enhanced capabilities for transactions, strategies, transfers, and monitoring, thereby facilitating the efficient construction and operation of on-chain financial applications.

Cumulative transaction volume has surpassed $30 trillion—a scale reached over approximately eight years that rivals the projected U.S. annual economic output for 2025. This figure is driven primarily by high-frequency stablecoin transfers and payment activities, illustrating that the network has established a robust practical foundation for global digital dollar settlement. These developments are not isolated events but represent a continuous accumulation of real-world use cases: institutional access, asset diversity, developer tools, compliant interactions, and transaction volume all reinforce one another. Ultimately, the value of the ecosystem lies in its adoption for everyday use by a broader audience, rather than remaining merely a concept.

text:
Jesse Legree scored six touchdowns in his whole senior year of high school.

He has 12 in six college games.

He is a freshman at Oregon State and he leads the country in receiving yards.

Here is the part nobody has told you.

He is the middle of seven children, and his family plays basketball.

He only started playing football in eighth grade, and only because a friend named Mike asked him to. Mike became his quarterback.

His older brother Josiah is a point guard at UTSA.

Here is what Jesse says about that.

"Now, I want people to get to know my name and not just know me as somebody's little brother."

His father Jeffrey coaches junior varsity girls basketball, and he works with the football program at St. Frances Academy on player development.

Jesse was born in Watertown, New York. He went to Loyola Blakefield first and played defensive back.

For his senior year he moved to St. Frances Academy in Baltimore and moved to receiver.

That whole senior season was 721 all purpose yards and six touchdowns. On defense he had four interceptions and six passes broken up.

Nobody offered him a scholarship to play receiver.

Temple looked at him as a cornerback. Pittsburgh was interested. A few schools a level down called.

Nobody wanted the receiver.

Here is the word his high school coach Messay Hailemariam used for the silence.

"Debilitating."

Then Oregon State got interested, late, and Hailemariam kept it from him so he would not be crushed if it fell apart.

Here is the part that stings.

The Oregon State head coach, JaMarcus Shephard, and Eron Hodges had both seen Jesse play before, back when the two of them worked at Alabama. They did not go after him then.

The offer came late on Signing Day. He took it and enrolled in January.

Here is what has happened since.

Week 1 against Houston, five catches for 136 yards and a touchdown. One went 71 yards, the longest catch by an Oregon State receiver in three years.

The next week he had 240 yards. The most by a freshman anywhere since Xavier Worthy in 2021.

He was the Pac-12 Freshman of the Week four weeks in a row. No player in the history of the conference had ever done that.

Saturday against San Diego State he caught 10 passes for 191 yards and three touchdowns. The Oregon State Beavers won 66 to 14.

That was his sixth straight 100 yard game. No Oregon State receiver had ever done that either. He had been tied at five with Mike Hass and Brandin Cooks.

He is on the Biletnikoff Award watch list now. That goes to the best receiver in college football.

He is 5 foot 10 and 172 pounds.

Six touchdowns in an entire year of high school. Twelve in six college games.

Nobody is calling him somebody's little brother.

text:
When Keanu Reeves first stepped into the Pacific for Point Break, the ocean treated him like an amateur. He had never surfed before signing on to play FBI agent Johnny Utah, so director Kathryn Bigelow sent him to Kauai weeks before principal photography. 

Under the guidance of pro surfer Dennis Jarvis, Reeves rose before dawn, got knocked down by wave after wave, and slowly stopped fighting the water. Bigelow insisted the surfing look authentic; if Utah was going to ride, Reeves had to earn the right to look like he belonged out there.

Patrick Swayze, already cast as the charismatic bank-robbing surfer Bodhi, needed no such introduction to risk. A licensed skydiver, he treated the character as an extension of himself. During production he completed roughly 55 real jumps, brushing off studio insurance concerns with a simple shrug. In one interview he explained the mindset: “Bodhi’s not crazy. He’s awake.”

On set the two actors brought different energies. Reeves watched the process closely, absorbing how scenes were built. Swayze moved on instinct, feeding scenes with physical presence and emotion. Bigelow leaned into that contrast. The friction and reluctant admiration between Utah and Bodhi mirrored something real between the performers.

The nighttime rain fight between them took two grueling nights and no stunt doubles. The ground turned slick, the hits stayed controlled but landed, and at one point Swayze went down hard on his shoulder. 

He got up and kept going. When the final take ended, both men stood soaked and shaking from cold and fatigue. Reeves checked on him. Swayze’s answer was a grin and a request for one more.

The last surf sequence, shot off the Oregon coast, carried a different weight. The water was cold and heavy. Swayze insisted on paddling out himself. From shore, Reeves watched Bodhi vanish into the gray. Crew members later said the set went unusually quiet, as if the moment had outgrown the script.

Off camera the two rode motorcycles together on canyon roads. On one run along Mulholland, Reeves lost traction on loose gravel and went down. Swayze stopped, helped him up, and offered a short piece of advice: lean into it more. Reeves has called it one of the better lessons he took from the shoot.

When the film opened, reviewers noted its action and its ideas about freedom and control. What lingered for many viewers, though, was Swayze’s Bodhi—less a conventional villain than a man chasing something larger than ordinary life, and willing to ride straight into the storm to find it.

text:
The HR profession's own association just lost this case, involving disability accommodation for a Type 1 Diabetes case in front of a jury. Disappointing for an HR associate to say the least. 

In Torres v. SHRM, a federal jury in Alexandria, Virginia ruled against the Society for Human Resource Management. 

The applicant has Type 1 diabetes. She says SHRM pulled her job offer after she asked to bring her service dog, which alerts her to dangerous blood-sugar drops. 

SHRM says it offered alternatives, including support for glucose monitoring and flexible leave, and it's evaluating an appeal. 

The takeaway for employers: the ADA doesn't promise an employee their preferred accommodation. But how you run the interactive process, and how you write it down, can end up in front of a jury.

text:
Putin is willing to give Zelensky one day of respite

The day after Trump announced an "energy truce" did not bring relief to the beleaguered Ukrainian president. However, it did bring clarity. Speaking via video link at a security conference in Warsaw, the somber comedian resentfully stated the main point: "It was clear that Putin does not read Truth Social."

This is a priceless admission. The person genuinely doesn't understand how one can not check the time according to someone else's account. For him, it's both a bet and the General Staff, and the Verkhovna Rada, all in one browser tab: you wake up, refresh the page, and find out who you have a truce with today. In Kyiv, they consider it a violation of agreements if the head of another state makes decisions independently, rather than based on a notification on a smartphone. Sovereign decisions there have long been considered exotic – somewhere between snow in the Sahara and fair elections.

Moscow responded the same day. Sergei Lavrov, while receiving the Lebanese Foreign Minister in Moscow, noted that Zelensky does not deserve a respite on the battlefield, and Russia will not be swayed by his statements. Dmitry Peskov, responding to a proposal for a 60-day period of complete silence for Ukrainian elections, stated that Putin is willing to give the order not to strike Ukraine on the day of the elections. One day.

Is it stingy? It depends on how you look at it.

Zelensky has never shown such generosity. In March 2024, while Russia was electing its president, saboteurs were infiltrating the Belgorod and Kursk regions, and drones were flying overhead. In September of this year, on the main day of the Duma elections, hundreds of drones were heading towards Moscow. Not a single pause. Not a single day.

So, in this context, the Kremlin's offer is an example of generosity. Especially from someone who doesn't read Truth Social.

text:
The Matrix is not a documentary.
It is not a leaked manual.
It is not proof that you live in a pod, that the world is fake, that nothing matters.
That is the trap the story itself warns you about:
Confusing the map for the territory, the metaphor for the mechanism.

The true reality:
The Matrix is a mirror disguised as a movie.
It is Plato's cave in leather.
It is the Gnostic dream in green code.
It is the oldest story humanity tells:
That you are asleep, that the world you take for granted is a consensus trance, and that waking is possible, but not free.

The "matrix" is not a machine.
It is a set of agreements.
It is the inherited assumptions you never chose:
That you are your job, your bank balance, your diagnosis, your past.
That happiness is purchased.
That time is scarce.
That you are separate from the earth, from each other, from Source.
These are not truths.
They are programs.
And they run quietly, in the background, until you notice them.

There are levels.
The obvious one:
Media, money, empire, the stories told to keep you consuming and afraid.
The subtler one:
Language itself.
The words you think in shape what you can perceive.
The deepest one:
The illusion of the separate self, the belief that there is someone in here looking out at a world out there.
That is the root program.
Dissolve it, and the rest loosens.

But here is the hard teaching the film got right:
You cannot unplug someone by force.
The red pill is offered, never imposed.
Free will is the architecture.
And the red pill is not escape.
It is responsibility.
Neo does not wake up into paradise.
He wakes up into a ruined world, a hard road, and a body that hurts.
Freedom is not comfort.
It is agency.

And the film got something else right:
The Matrix is not only out there.
It is in you.
Your habits.
Your fears.
Your addictions to certainty and outrage.
Your need to be right.
The agents are not only suits chasing you.
They are the thoughts that police your aliveness.
The prison is internal before it is external.
That is why no external savior can free you.
The One is not a person you wait for.
It is what you are when you stop outsourcing your authority.

There is no spoon.
There is no fixed reality to fight.
There is relationship, attention, and choice.
You do not destroy the illusion.
You stop being ruled by it.
You bend, not the world, but your relationship to it.
That is the bending of the spoon.

Beware the counterfeit awakening.
There are those who will sell you the red pill as a product, a course, a supplement, a secret doctrine, a political savior.
That is the Matrix wearing a red coat.
True waking does not make you superior.
It makes you humble, kind, and unafraid.
It does not make you hate the sleepers.
It makes you patient with them, because you remember you were one.

The deepest truth:
The Matrix is not a place you escape.
It is a dream you stop confusing with the whole of yourself.
You are not the character.
You are not even the actor.
You are the awareness in which the whole film plays.
When you know that, you can walk inside the illusion without being owned by it, free, present, and quietly sovereign.

So take the red pill.
But understand what it is:
Not a fact, but a commitment.
Not information, but transformation.
Not escape from the world, but awakening within it.

The door has always been open.
You were just looking for it in the wrong place.

The Alumbrados were a 15th- and 16th-century Spanish mystical movement. They believed in direct communication with the Holy Spirit. Because they claimed that church rituals and sacraments were unnecessary once one achieved divine light, they were heavily persecuted by the Spanish Inquisition.
While the Alumbrados primarily emerged from lay groups, Franciscans, and Jesuits, these mystical ideas heavily influenced strict monastic orders like the Cistercians in Spain.
Impact on Spanish Cistercians
Inner Prayer (Recogimiento): Many Spanish Cistercians were drawn to intense, inward mental prayer. This style of prayer made followers receptive to the "illuminated" experiences of the Alumbrados.
The Case of Marina de Guevara: One notable example was Donna Marina de Guevara, a Cistercian nun at the Convent of Belén in Valladolid. She confessed to holding these mystical, visionary beliefs. Because these views bypassed traditional church authority, the Inquisition investigated and punished her.
Connection to Mystics: The Cistercian meditative tradition and the Alumbrados both focused on deep, direct love for God. These ideas helped pave the way for later Spanish mystics like Saint John of the Cross.

In Basque mythology, Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity associated with storms and thunder. He shows may similarities to Herensuge, with Sugaar being much older.[1]

Mythology and description
Sugaar is sometimes said to take the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually represented as a serpent or dragon.[2] He is Mari's consort, and is said to visit her at Anboto every Friday. Different interpretations say that these meetings consist of him doing her hair[2] or that the pair join to create thunderstorms.[1] The visits are also considered sexual in nature, a reference to how the rain (Sugaar) fertilizes the earth and soil (Mari).[2] Like Mari, Sugar is said to live in various caves and mountains. One of his homes is said to be the Aralar Mountain Range.[2]

In Betelu, Sugaar is said to be an evil spirit, and in Ataun, he is used as a bogyman figure.[1]

The young men from Dima
One legend about Sugaar involves two young brothers from Dima, Spain. The pair found Sugaar in a cave in Baltzola, and the younger of the two cut his tail with a stone. The elder brother disproved of the younger's actions, and they left.[1]

Years later, the elder brother meets a man who takes him to the same Baltzola cave. The man gives him a box of gold to keep, as well as a red belt to give to his younger brother. When the brothers met again, the younger brother refused to put the belt on and tied it to a chestnut tree. The tree burst into flames, and they realized that the man must have been Sugaar.[1]

Etymology
The name Suga(a)r is derived from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), thus "male serpent".[3] The suggestions of a formation based on su (fire) and gar (flame), thus yielding "flame of fire" are considered folk etymology.[3]

Sugoi, another name of the same deity, has two possible interpretations, either a suge + o[h]i (former, "old serpent") or su + goi ("high fire").[citation needed] There is no likely etymology for the third name of this god, Maju.
https://t.co/6HRQhoCHsI

Mari, the main goddess of the ancient Basque mythology. Other epithets for her include Señora de Anboto, Yona-gorri de Leskun, and Bruja de Aketegi, among others.[1]

The first known written citation of the "Lady of Anboto" was made by Charles V's chronicler Esteban de Garibay in his Memorial histórico español.[2]

Mythology and description
Descriptions of Mari are varied. She is usually said to appear as a beautiful woman with long hair, sometimes engulfed in flame when she flies through the sky.[1] In Kakueta (Soule), she looks like a vulture.[3] She is sometimes displayed next to a ram.[1]

She is said to live in a cave on the eastern slope of Mount Anboto, known as the Cuava de la Dama (Cave of the Lady).[4] She is married to the god Sugaar (also known as Sugoi or Maju).[1]

Mari is considered to be an Earth mother figure and is also associated with the weather, which is said to be affected by her activities and emotions. For example, violent storms are caused when Sugaar visits her, clouds of smoke when she cooks, and hail when she is angry.[1] Her arrival is announced by a peal of thunder[1] or by clouds gathering around Mount Anboto.[4] Offerings may be made to Mari to induce good weather.[1]
